title: La femme publique
description: The screening on August 23rd will be introduced by writer Daniel Bird. The screening on October 1st will be introduced by…

title: Radiohead X Nosferatu: A Symphony of Horror
description: Silents Synced pairs classic silent movies with epic rock music to bring audiences a unique big screen experience. This reimagining of the iconic Nosferatu (1922) features Radiohead’s Kid A (2000) and Amnesiac (2001) albums. An unauthorized adaptation of Bram Stoker’s Dracula, Nosferatu (1922) is the quintessential silent vampire film, crafted by legendary German director F. W. Murnau. Rather than depicting Dracula as a shape-shifting monster or debonair gentleman, Murnau’s Graf Orlok (as portrayed by Max Schreck) is a nightmarish, spidery creature of bulbous head and taloned claws - perhaps the most genuinely disturbing incarnation of vampirism yet envisioned. Don’t miss out on the chance to experience this imaginative new take on an iconic horror classic!

title: Off-Circuit: The Seasons
description: Weaving accounts of rural workers and field notes of a couple of archaeologists, amateur footage and scientific drawings, legends, poems and songs, Maureen Fazendeiro's The Seasons is a journey through the real history and the tales of a region in southern Portugal, Alentejo, and a portrait of the people who have lived there.

title: The Silence of the Lambs
description: Jodie Foster stars as Clarice Starling, a top student at the FBI's training academy. Jack Crawford (Scott Glenn) wants Clarice to interview Dr. Hannibal Lecter (Anthony Hopkins), a brilliant psychiatrist who is also a violent psychopath, serving life behind bars for various acts of murder and cannibalism. Crawford believes that Lecter may have insight into a case and that Starling, as an attractive young woman, may be just the bait to draw him out.

title: Birth
description: It took Anna (Nicole Kidman) 10 years to recover from the death of her husband, Sean, but now she's on the verge of marrying her boyfriend, Joseph (Danny Huston), and finally moving on. However, on the night of her engagement party, a young boy named Sean (Cameron Bright) turns up, saying he is her dead husband reincarnated. At first she ignores the child, but his knowledge of her former husband's life is uncanny, leading her to believe that he might be telling the truth.

title: The Shining [UK Version]
description: Jack Torrance (Jack Nicholson) becomes winter caretaker at the isolated Overlook Hotel in Colorado, hoping to cure his writer's block. He settles in along with his wife, Wendy (Shelley Duvall), and his son, Danny (Danny Lloyd), who is plagued by psychic premonitions. As Jack's writing goes nowhere and Danny's visions become more disturbing, Jack discovers the hotel's dark secrets and begins to unravel into a homicidal maniac hell-bent on terrorizing his family.

title: The Blair Witch Project
description: Found video footage tells the tale of three film students (Heather Donahue, Joshua Leonard, Michael C. Williams) who've traveled to a small town to collect documentary footage about the Blair Witch, a legendary local murderer. Over the course of several days, the students interview townspeople and gather clues to support the tale's veracity. But the project takes a frightening turn when the students lose their way in the woods and begin hearing horrific noises.

title: Yi Yi
description: The extraordinary, internationally embraced Yi Yi (A One and a Two . . .), directed by the late Taiwanese master Edward Yang, follows a middle-class family in Taipei over the course of one year, beginning with a wedding and ending with a funeral. Whether chronicling middle-age father NJ’s tentative flirtations with an old flame or precocious young son Yang-Yang’s attempts at capturing reality with his beloved camera, the filmmaker deftly imbues every gorgeous frame with a compassionate clarity. Warm, sprawling, and dazzling, this intimate epic is one of the undisputed masterworks of the new century. 4K digital restoration carried out by Pony Canyon Inc., with analog and digital processes provided by Imagica Entertainment Media Services, Inc.

title: Scream
description: Wes Craven re-invented and revitalised the slasher-horror genre with this modern horror classic, which manages to be funny, clever and scary, as a fright-masked knife maniac stalks high-school students in middle-class suburbia. Craven is happy to provide both tension and self-parody as the body count mounts - but the victims aren't always the ones you'd expect.

title: Nosferatu
description: This performance will feature a live score performed by Hugo Max . "I first saw Murnau’s Symphony of Horror when I was nine years old. The film’s expressionistic images continue to haunt me, the chiaroscuro compositions tapping vividly into timeless subconscious fears. My improvisations on viola and piano draw inspiration from the leitmotifs and sound effects of 70s horror soundtracks and the languages of Second Viennese School composers contemporary to Murnau, also Jewish Traditional Music that informs my personal approach to creating a score for the film." - Hugo Max Please view this YouTube video for a sample of Hugo's work. Photo Credit - Richard Ecclestone An iconic film of the German expressionist cinema, and one of the most famous of all silent movies, F. W. Murnau's Nosferatu: A Symphony of Horror continues to haunt — and, indeed, terrify — modern audiences with the unshakable power of its images. By teasing a host of occult atmospherics out of dilapidated set-pieces and innocuous real-world locations alike, Murnau captured on celluloid the deeply-rooted elements of a waking nightmare, and launched the signature "Murnau-style" that would change cinema history forever. In this first-ever screen adaptation of Bram Stoker's Dracula, a simple real-estate transaction leads an intrepid businessman deep into the superstitious heart of Transylvania. There he encounters the otherworldly Count Orlok — portrayed by the legendary Max Schreck, in a performance the very backstory of which has spawned its own mythology — who soon after embarks upon a cross-continental voyage to take up residence in a distant new land... and establish his ambiguous dominion. As to whether the count's campaign against the plague-wracked populace erupts from satanic decree, erotic compulsion, or the simple impulse of survival — that remains, perhaps, the greatest mystery of all in this film that's like a blackout...

title: Kikuyu Land + Q&A
description: The screening will be followed by a Q&A with Kenyan director/protagonist Bea Wangondu and protagonist Mr Mungai. While investigating a local…

title: The Texas Chain Saw Massacre
description: When Sally (Marilyn Burns) hears that her grandfather's grave may have been vandalized, she and her paraplegic brother, Franklin (Paul A. Partain), set out with their friends to investigate. After a detour to their family's old farmhouse, they discover a group of crazed, murderous outcasts living next door. As the group is attacked one by one by the chainsaw-wielding Leatherface (Gunnar Hansen), who wears a mask of human skin, the survivors must do everything they can to escape.

title: ALANIS
description: Set in Argentina, ALANIS navigates the life of a single sex working parent. Though Alanis faces a deluge of problems with clients that plague every woman selling sex, the real threat to her security and the safety of her child stems from the social workers and laws that construct obstacles under the guise of protecting “precarious” women and children.

title: COMBAT BREATHING: THE TIME BENEATH THE CONCRETE
description: “I’m in jail out here, I’m in jail in there.” –Hugh Masekela The prison is the institutionalization of a logic central to the systemic formation and reproduction of racial capitalism and colonialism. It remains the primary form in modernity through which states (either under ostensibly opposing but in truth co-constituting liberal democratic and fascistic guises) manage surplus populations, extract surplus value, break social and kinship relations, and utilize the captive body to control not only those within its walls, but also those on the outside. This film program borrows its title – and something of its poetic and conceptual grammar – from the writing of scholar Nasser Abourahme, who in his book “The Time Beneath the Concrete” brings the prison into immediate relation with the colony and the refugee camp in Palestine. Extending his analysis to the ghetto and the reservation within the U.S. context as additional sites of enclosure, this program with works by Alex Johnston, Sky Hopinka, and Larry Clark attends not only to the violence of imprisonment, but also to the ways such sites have and continue to be made into focal points of struggle by those whose lives they seek to crush and mold. What emerges is a transnational, historically grounded, and situated account of the carceral system that traces the prison’s many reinventions while insisting that the project of enclosure, however violently renewed, is never complete. Alex Johnston EVIDENCE OF THE EVIDENCE (2018, 20 min, DCP) The 1971 Attica Prison Rebellion remains a defining moment of radical resistance – not only in the history of prison struggles and the American anti-racist and anti-state movement, but also for international struggles against enclosure and carcerality. The state’s retaking of the prison on the fourth and final day of the uprising, described as the bloodiest one-day encounter between Americans since the Civil War, remains an open wound. EVIDENCE OF THE EVIDENCE examines this fraught and contested history through a granular interrogation of the archival record. Drawing on previously unseen video footage recorded by a state trooper during the four-day rebellion, the film offers a visceral, ground-level account of the events at Attica while tracing how they were simultaneously mediated and narrativized through the images being produced. Recalling Harun Farocki and Andrei Ujică’s seminal VIDEOGRAMS OF A REVOLUTION (1992), the film considers the manifold roles moving images play in producing history and memory – as well as in their erasure and destruction. At a moment of escalating racism and authoritarianism across the West, when prisons and other regimes of enclosure remain indispensable to imperial domination, EVIDENCE OF THE EVIDENCE emerges as a timely and urgent work of agitprop and media criticism. Sky Hopinka SUNFLOWER SIEGE ENGINE (2022, 12 min, DCP) The Occupation of Alcatraz (1969-71) marked a historic moment of indigenous resistance in the United States. Led by Indians of All Tribes (IAT), eighty-nine Native activists and their supporters occupied the abandoned federal prison island, demanding self-determination, tribal sovereignty, and land rights, forcefully recentering the question of indigenous land against the settler-colonial foundations of the U.S. empire. Although the occupation also brought to the fore the many unresolved contradictions within pan-Indian political discourse and organizing, particularly around the contested meanings of sovereignty and indigeneity, its memory and legacy continue to offer a vital site of reflection and empowerment in struggles for land and decolonization. In SUNFLOWER SIEGE ENGINE, distinct moments and scales of resistance are collapsed and woven together: documentation of the Alcatraz occupation; the reclamation of Cahokia and the repatriation of ancestors; and intimate reflections on inhabiting one’s body in the present while looking back upon historical struggles and their continuities, excesses, and impasses. Through experimental visual gestures and poetry, the film meditates on the carceral origins and enduring logic of the reservation system, asking where sovereignty and belligerence converge, and where they break away. Larry Clark AS ABOVE, SO BELOW (1973, 52 min, 16mm-to-DCP) One of the most politically radical films to emerge from the L.A. Rebellion, AS ABOVE, SO BELOW offers an uncompromising portrayal of the formation of revolutionary consciousness, the underground organization of black insurgency in the United States, and the place of these processes within the broader project of Third World liberation. The film centers on Jita-Hadi, who grows up in the structurally abandoned neighborhoods of postwar Chicago. He later joins the Marine Corps, only to become disillusioned when he is deployed across Asia and the Caribbean to suppress leftist governments and protect U.S. imperial and capitalist interests. Returning to an increasingly ghettoized United States, Jita-Hadi is discreetly recruited into a black insurrectionary group. The narrative is interwoven with archival radio broadcasts and film excerpts that evoke the carceral state’s suppression of racialized groups, as well as parodic scenes – including narcotizing church services and the monologues of a black centrist. Through these different registers, the film sharply articulates the internal and external, national and transnational obstacles confronting black liberation. Total running time: ca. 90 min.

title: Shadows of Beirut + Q&A
description: This screening will be followed by a Q&A. A young woman decides to return to Beirut to see her estranged dying…

title: The Cremator
description: All screenings feature a recorded introduction from curator and scholar of Eastern European cult cinema Daniel Bird. Juraj Herz's film The…

title: Mulholland Dr.
description: A dark-haired woman (Laura Elena Harring) is left amnesiac after a car crash. She wanders the streets of Los Angeles in a daze before taking refuge in an apartment. There she is discovered by Betty (Naomi Watts), a wholesome Midwestern blonde who has come to the City of Angels seeking fame as an actress. Together, the two attempt to solve the mystery of Rita's true identity. The story is set in a dream-like Los Angeles, spoilt neither by traffic jams nor smog.

title: MOMMY IS COMING
description: When the woes of monogamy affect the queer sex life of Dylan and Claudia, the couple enlist the help of sex professionals to reinvigorate their passion. These professionals range from the dominatrixes of the underground nightclub dungeons in Berlin to the sex educational help of Dylan’s mom. Through these sexcapades the women learn about their self-esteem, libido, and all the ways in which they become their mothers.

title: FFC: The Songbird's Secret (U*)
description: An enchanting feature-length animation made entirely from cut paper.

title: The Princess and the Frog
description: In New Orleans during the Jazz Age, a beautiful girl named Tiana (Anika Noni Rose) dreams of owning her own restaurant.…

title: Tampopo
description: The tale of an eccentric band of culinary ronin who guide the widow of a noodle-shop owner on her quest for the perfect recipe, this rapturous “ramen western” by Japanese director Juzo Itami is an entertaining, genre-bending adventure underpinned by a deft satire of the way social conventions distort the most natural of human urges—our appetites. Interspersing the efforts of Tampopo (Nobuko Miyamoto) and friends to make her café a success with the erotic exploits of a gastronome gangster and glimpses of food culture both high and low, the sweet, sexy, and surreal Tampopo is a lavishly inclusive paean to the sensual joys of nourishment, and one of the most mouthwatering examples of food on film ever made.

title: Jurassic Park
description: In Steven Spielberg's massive blockbuster, paleontologists Alan Grant (Sam Neill) and Ellie Sattler (Laura Dern) and mathematician Ian Malcolm (Jeff Goldblum) are among a select group chosen to tour an island theme park populated by dinosaurs created from prehistoric DNA. While the park's mastermind, billionaire John Hammond (Richard Attenborough), assures everyone that the facility is safe, they find out otherwise when various ferocious predators break free and go on the hunt.

title: HKFF: I am fine, thank you. + Panel Discussion
London Latino Film Festival presents: Espina + Intro
description: Espina is a vibrant comedy-drama by Daniel Poler inspired by the real-life experiences of its lead actor, Jonathan Benaim. Before undergoing spinal…

title: The Lost Boys
description: Teenage brothers Michael (Jason Patric) and Sam (Corey Haim) move with their mother (Dianne Wiest) to a small town in northern California. While the younger Sam meets a pair of kindred spirits in geeky comic-book nerds Edward (Corey Feldman) and Alan (Jamison Newlander), the angst-ridden Michael soon falls for Star (Jami Gertz) -- who turns out to be in thrall to David (Kiefer Sutherland), leader of a local gang of vampires. Sam and his new friends must save Michael and Star from the undead.

title: Event Horizon
description: Captain Miller and his team discover unbelievable secrets when they board the Event Horizon, a starship that had mysteriously disappeared during its maiden voyage, which puts their lives in danger.

title: COMBAT BREATHING: PERPETUAL RECURRENCES, PART 1: CINÉ-GUERRILLAS
description: What characterizes the militant image? What historical conditions produced it and what kinds of histories were, in turn, produced by it? Where might it be found today? This program brings together a selection of contemporary works that frontally engage the legacies and continuities of Third Cinema and the tricontinental geographies of leftist, anti-colonial collaboration and mobilization that were this cultural movement’s primary condition of possibility. These works, as with Third Cinema, refuse clear-cut divisions between formal acuity and socio-political signification, and ground cinema’s documentative, archival, and imaginative powers as useful tools in the ongoing decolonizing process. Such a process involves grappling with the positive and negative lessons of prior movements in order to deduce alternative pathways to liberation. The selected films in this program revisit various sites of unfinished and unfolding anti-colonial struggle, from Ghana and Palestine to Yugoslavia and Algeria. Orienting viewers toward critical reflections on the historical twists and turns of the capitalist world-system on macro and interpersonal scales while remaining firmly rooted in their respective presents, the works by Mila Turajlić, John Akomfrah with Black Audio Film Collective, and Reem Shilleh further articulate the persisting structures of colonialism in their intensifications and mutations following from these mid-twentieth-century decolonization movements. The continuity of said conditions into this millennium can only ever engender, as these films themselves embody, the “perpetual recurrence” of a countervailing militant image. Mila Turajlić CINÉ-GUERRILLAS: SCENES FROM THE LABUDOVIĆ REELS 2022, 94 min, DCP Based on resurrected 35mm footage shot by Stevan Labudović, the official cameraman of former Yugoslav President Tito, this documentary by Mila Turajlić takes viewers on an archival road trip through the insurgent historical streams and collaborative Third World networks that constituted and sustained the Algerian anti-colonial struggle from 1954-62. Turajlić follows Labudović’s work in Algeria through intimate interviews with him and Algerian revolutionary contemporaries, matching his newsreel footage – audiovisual testaments to tricontinental solidarity – with excerpts from his diary. Employing only images of the Algerian War not shown from a French perspective, CINÉ-GUERRILLAS wades through the media and propaganda battle that played out during the liberation struggle, where cinema was mobilized as a political weapon of resistance against colonialism and empire as well as a social, imaginative medium of world-making.

title: KAMA SUTRA: A TALE OF LOVE
description: In KAMA SUTRA: A TALE OF LOVE, Mira Nair examines the stigmatization of sexually promiscuous and unmarried women by the upper class in 16th-century India. The film follows Maya, a servant, who embarks on a journey of self-discovery through the art and spiritual practice of being a courtesan. Though ultimately a film about love, as signaled in the title, the film presents a rare historical fictional account of the spiritual art of working sex in the 16th-century.

title: Halloween (1978)
description: Fifteen years after murdering his sister on Halloween Night 1963, Michael Myers escapes from a mental hospital and returns to the small town of Haddonfield, Illinois to kill again.

title: In the Mouth of Madness
description: When horror novelist Sutter Cane (Jürgen Prochnow) goes missing, insurance investigator John Trent (Sam Neill) scrutinizes the claim made by his publisher, Jackson Harglow (Charlton Heston), and endeavors to retrieve a yet-to-be-released manuscript and ascertain the writer's whereabouts. Accompanied by the novelist's editor, Linda Styles (Julie Carmen), and disturbed by nightmares from reading Cane's other novels, Trent makes an eerie nighttime trek to a supernatural town in New Hampshire.

title: COMBAT BREATHING: PERPETUAL RECURRENCES, PART 2: TESTAMENT
description: What characterizes the militant image? What historical conditions produced it and what kinds of histories were, in turn, produced by it? Where might it be found today? This program brings together a selection of contemporary works that frontally engage the legacies and continuities of Third Cinema and the tricontinental geographies of leftist, anti-colonial collaboration and mobilization that were this cultural movement’s primary condition of possibility. The continuity of said conditions into this millennium can only ever engender, as these films themselves embody, the “perpetual recurrence” of a countervailing militant image. John Akomfrah & Black Audio Film Collective TESTAMENT 1988, 80 min, 16mm-to-DCP TESTAMENT is among the earliest feature-length works created by the pioneering UK-based art group, Black Audio Film Collective (of which John Akomfrah was a founding member). Synthesizing the languages of Third Cinema and avant-garde montage with the lamentational affects of postcolonial disillusionment, TESTAMENT offers a probing spectral meditation on the condition of the African postcolony. The film’s protagonist, Abena, is an exiled activist turned television reporter who returns to Ghana two decades after the 1966 coup that brought an end to President Kwame Nkrumah’s experiment in Pan-African socialism. Adrift in a “war zone of memories,” Abena is caught in the cleavage between public history and private memory. Characteristic of the collective’s now-signature blend of archival documents, fictional sequences, and layered sound scores, TESTAMENT enfolds depopulated frames, frigid tones, allegories of mourning, and a cast of enigmatic characters to evoke an emotional landscape of loss and arrested political possibility. Introduced by Christian Nyampeta.

title: HKFF: Forms of the (Un)erasable: Moving Image + Lecture Performance
FUCKTOYS
description: Set in the alternate universe of Trashtown (but filmed in the American South), Annapurna Sriram’s debut feature film FUCKTOYS is a surrealist queer black comedy about a young woman on a mission to break a curse. Throughout a chaotic 24-hour journey, the protagonist (and her compatriots) navigate the intersecting oppressive systems of capitalism that make hustlers out of us all in pursuit of a spiritual, if not ecstatic, release of the body and soul.

title: On the Silver Globe
description: The screening on August 22nd will feature an introduction by writer Daniel Bird. Subsequent screenings of On the Silver Globe will feature…

title: There Will Be Blood
description: Ruthless silver miner, turned oil prospector, Daniel Plainview moves to oil-rich California. Using his adopted son HW to project a trustworthy, family-man image, Plainview cons local landowners into selling him their valuable properties for a pittance. However, local preacher Eli Sunday suspects Plainviews motives and intentions, starting a slow-burning feud that threatens both their lives.

title: COMBAT BREATHING: PERPETUAL RECURRENCES, PART 3: PERPETUAL RECURRENCES
description: What characterizes the militant image? What historical conditions produced it and what kinds of histories were, in turn, produced by it? Where might it be found today? The continuity of said conditions into this millennium can only ever engender, as these films themselves embody, the “perpetual recurrence” of a countervailing militant image. Reem Shilleh PERPETUAL RECURRENCES 2016, 60 min, DCP A meta-reflection on the militant image and its contemporary reappearances, PERPETUAL RECURRENCES montages scenes extracted from numerous films and videos created over the last four decades by Palestinians and about Palestine, tracking thematic, gestural, and compositional repetitions between works produced during the Palestinian revolutionary period of 1968-82, the period following the 1993 Oslo Accords, and the volatile twenty-first century. Through Reem Shilleh’s methodical stitching together of repeating filmic occurrences – with respect to location, political discourse, mise-en-scene, objects, and so on – various scenes become unfixed from their narrative contexts and historical conditions, inviting expansive associations and haunting correspondences. Meandering in a seemingly improvised fashion between cinematic fragments of classroom instruction and conversing militants gathered under trees to handheld camera shots of refugee camps and moving car shots of streets, checkpoints, and landscapes, Shilleh’s vast media traversal materializes an equally lyrical and deconstructive reimagination of exercises in film programming. Introduced by Tiffany Malakooti.

title: Possession
description: After Anna (Isabelle Adjani) reveals to her husband, Mark (Sam Neill), that she is having an affair, she leaves him and their son. Mark is devastated, and seeks out Heinrich (Heinz Bennent), the man who cuckolded him, only to receive a beating. After a series of violent confrontations between Mark and Anna, Mark hires a private investigator to follow her. Anna descends into madness, and it's soon clear that she is hiding a much bigger secret -- one that is both inexplicable and shocking.

title: The Princess and the Frog
description: In New Orleans during the Jazz Age, a beautiful girl named Tiana (Anika Noni Rose) dreams of owning her own restaurant.…

title: Young Frankenstein
description: Respected medical lecturer Dr. Frederick Frankenstein (Gene Wilder) learns that he has inherited his infamous grandfather's estate in Transylvania. Arriving at the castle, Dr. Frankenstein soon begins to recreate his grandfather's experiments with the help of servants Igor (Marty Feldman), Inga (Teri Garr) and the fearsome Frau Blücher (Cloris Leachman). After he creates his own monster (Peter Boyle), new complications ensue with the arrival of the doctor's fiancée, Elizabeth (Madeline Kahn).

title: Perfect Blue
description: "THE COLOUR OF ILLUSION IS PERFECT BLUE" A young Japanese singer is encouraged by her agent to quit singing and pursue an acting career, beginning with a role in a murder mystery TV show.

title: Barry Lyndon
description: Stanley Kubrick bent the conventions of the historical drama to his own will in this dazzling vision of a pitiless aristocracy, adapted from a novel by William Makepeace Thackeray. In picaresque detail, Barry Lyndon chronicles the adventures of an incorrigible trickster (Ryan O’Neal) whose opportunism takes him from an Irish farm to the battlefields of the Seven Years’ War and the parlours of high society. For the most sumptuously crafted film of his career, Kubrick recreated the decadent surfaces and intricate social codes of the period, evoking the light and texture of eighteenth-century painting with the help of pioneering cinematographic techniques and lavish costume and production design, all of which earned Academy Awards. The result is a masterpiece—a sardonic, devastating portrait of a vanishing world whose opulence conceals the moral vacancy at its heart. Please Note: The film will be presented with a brief 5-10min intermission.

title: Suspiria [1977]
description: Suzy (Jessica Harper) travels to Germany to attend ballet school. When she arrives, late on a stormy night, no one lets her in, and she sees Pat (Eva Axén), another student, fleeing from the school. When Pat reaches her apartment, she is murdered. The next day, Suzy is admitted to her new school, but has a difficult time settling in. She hears noises, and often feels ill. As more people die, Suzy uncovers the terrifying secret history of the place.

title: AVATARS: THE DOMINATRIX SLEEPS TONIGHT
description: Taking the avatar of the dominatrix as its starting point, this short film program gathers together various films made – across a 40-year period – by or in collaboration with those who have experience in the leathersex scene. As an avatar of working sex, the figure of the dominatrix is elusive in so far as she uses the theater of the scene of “violation” to both pursue and obfuscate her desires. Though cinema longs to unmask the dominatrix to witness her “true” self, this program instead finds pleasure in the artifice of the scene wherein various characters find themselves at the mercy of the seductive and controlling gaze of the dominatrix. The shorts here range from documentary exercises of sadism, like Ione Wang’s WHEN I LOOK AT YOU, I SEE ME, to the electric pop-music video work of Beth B’s THE DOMINATRIX SLEEPS TONIGHT, made for the band Dominatrix. Shorts by Azian Nurudin and Michelle Handelman from the late 1980s and early 1990s invite a reconsideration of race, power, and aesthetics through their respectively overlooked and censored films, while M.M. Serra and Maria Beatty’s work demonstrates the aesthetic bliss that emerges from submitting to the fantasies of a powerful woman. Azian Nurudin NANCY’S NIGHTMARE (1988, 5 min, digital) Michelle Handelman CATSCAN (1989, 6 min, Super-8mm-to-digital. Made with with Monte Cazazza.) M.M. Serra & Jennifer Reeves DARLING INTERNATIONAL (1999, 22 min, 16mm-to-digital) Maria Beatty THE BLACK GLOVE (1996, 30 min, digital) Beth B THE DOMINATRIX SLEEPS TONIGHT (1984, 4 min, video) Ione Wang WHEN I LOOK AT YOU, I SEE ME (2024, 7 min, digital) Total running time: ca. 80 min.

title: CF75: Blanche
description: Contemporary Films 75th Anniversary Walerian Borowczyk’s critically acclaimed and influential medieval tale — a beautiful tragedy told with pitch-black humour and the director’s remarkable idiosyncratic inventiveness. Arguably Borowczyk’s most ambitious film, a meticulous recreation of medieval life by way of references from the history of art, not least Giotto’s religious paintings. Occupying the space between Pasolini and Parajanov as a sort of flat, two-dimensional moving tapestry, Blanche is based on a drama by the great Polish romantic poet Juliusz Słowacki, Mazepa. Featuring one of the last performances by the Swiss actor Michel Simon, not to mention a spirited turn by the late Jacques Perrin (also serving as an uncredited producing partner here), Blanche herself is played by Ligia Branice as a Sadean stock character whose innocent gothic beauty evokes male lust inevitably followed by bloody violence. While Borowczyk was able to realize his medieval masterpiece with complete artistic control, Blanche was a critical if not commercial success in France, but fared much better during Contemporary’s British run where it played for 20 weeks at Contemporary’s Paris Pullman cinema alone. Enthusiasts included documentary filmmaker Leslie Megahey, whose own Schalcken the Painter (1979) it influenced, Monty Python’s Terry Jones and Terry Gilliam (the latter cited the film, along with Pasolini, as key references when conjuring the medieval onscreen in Monty Python and the Holy Grail and Jabberwocky ), and the novelist and critic Marina Warner, who included Blanche in her study of fairy tales From the Beast to the Blonde . More than half a century later, two aspects of the film remain particularly striking: the way Borowczyk creates a flat, face-on world, like an animated tapestry, and its soundtrack, which set out to reconstruct the sound of authentic 13th-century musical instruments. The screening will be introduced by Daniel Bird, Co-founder of Friends of Walerian Borowczyk , a non-profit association based in Paris that manages the rights to the painter, sculptor and filmmaker. He will discuss Borowczyk’s association with Contemporary, and will be joined by Kathleen Wallfisch, Music Supervisor for film and TV, to talk about the music of the film and how it is arranged and presented on screen.

title: London Latino Film Festival presents: Querido trópico (Beloved Tropic)
description: Querido Trópico is a drama by Ana Endara that explores the unexpected connection between two women from different backgrounds brought together by…

title: COMBAT BREATHING: POSTSCRIPTS OF MODERNITY, PART 1
description: POSTSCRIPTS OF MODERNITY, PART 1 The promises and outcomes of modernity – nation-states and capitalist economies, along with their alienating and extractivist logics and infrastructures – have produced immeasurable catastrophic damage to peoples and living environments across racial and class lines. Throughout their reign, these violent systems have not simply been justified by the values of universality, individual freedom, and liberal secular democracy; they have been produced through them, eliminating and exploiting all that does not measure up or conform to their suffocating parameters. Central to modernity, and to modern discourse more broadly, is the capture of technology as a transhistorical practice and its transformation into a supposedly modern conception governed by the logic of progress. “Postscripts of Modernity” is a film program that engages these catastrophic and violent legacies while demonstrating how film, itself a modern technology, might visualize and facilitate other social relations – in other words, how existing at-hand technologies, currently governed by the reign of capital, might be appropriated and subverted to achieve ends nonsynchronous with their intended uses. The works by Hong Kong Documentary Filmmakers, Bahar Noorizadeh, and Nadir Bouhmouch disavow modernity’s violence not by returning to an imagined precolonial or precapitalist past, but by insisting on a kind of crude presentism. Their diverse aesthetic interventions within the political contexts they respectively work in embrace whatever tools are currently available within modernity as material for the struggle against it. Hong Kong Documentary Filmmakers TAKING BACK THE LEGISLATURE 2020, 45 min, DCP July 1, 2019 – the 22nd anniversary of Hong Kong’s handover to China after the end of British Imperial Rule – marks a critical moment in the region, considered, on the one hand, as a celebration of the establishment of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region and, on the other, as an occasion of mourning, anger, and mounting political frustration for pro-democracy groups, eventually culminating in an unprecedented act of social upheaval. As protesters question the effectiveness of months of non-violent demonstrations against the proposed extradition law, a group begins to contemplate a more radical course of action: storming the Legislative Council. Filmed from within the movement by anonymous filmmakers on handheld cameras, TAKING BACK THE LEGISLATURE follows the protesters through the escalating hours of confrontation. The camera captures heated debates among demonstrators over the risks of occupying the building, as well as their encounters with pro-democracy legislators who urge them to reconsider their actions. As frustration gives way to determination, protesters equipped with helmets, masks, and makeshift tools eventually break through the Legislative Council’s defenses and enter the chamber. Bahar Noorizadeh AFTER SCARCITY 2018, 30 min, DCP Can computational utopias offer a way out of the techno-capitalist monopolization of the present? In the Soviet Union of the 1960s, cyberneticians imagined computers as machines of communism, and cybernetics as a way to address the mounting difficulties of the planned economy. AFTER SCARCITY follows cyberneticians such as Viktor Glushkov, among others, who proposed that networked computers could overcome the vast bureaucratic inefficiencies of central planning and make possible a fully automated planned economy. If history, at its best, is a blueprint for science fiction, then revisiting these contingent histories of economic technology might open a path to the future beyond the speculative binds of the capitalist order. The work reconstructs this socialist cybernetic history through a deliberately futuristic visual language. Digitally generated landscapes, partly built from LiDAR scans, move through swarms of floating points that trace monasteries and city streets, compressing decades of history into a speculative space. These contingent pasts become prototypes for fictive futures, suggesting that digital socialism was not alien to the communist project, and that computation need not condemn us to the techno-capitalist present. The result is less a conventional historical documentary than a simulation of an alternative technological history with the past appearing as a prototype for a future that never arrived. Total running time: ca. 80 min. Introduced by Harris Chowdhary.

title: The Cabinet of Dr. Caligari (Live Score)
description: This performance will feature a live score performed by Hugo Max The rich timbre of the viola perfectly captures the aura of Robert Wiene's The Cabinet of Dr. Caligari. My improvisations translate the film's angular painted shadows into unnerving melodies inspired by musical techniques that were evolving during the 1920s. The nefarious showmanship of Caligari invites theatrical and macabre sounds, in contrast with ghostly gestures evoking ‘the somnambulist' who is compelled to act against his will. THE CABINET OF DR. CALIGARI : One of the most iconic masterpieces in cinema history, Robert Wiene's Das Cabinet des Dr Caligari shook filmgoers worldwide and changed the direction of the art form. Now presented in a definitive restoration, the film's chilling, radically expressionist vision is set to grip viewers again. At a local carnival in a small German town, hypnotist Dr. Caligari presents the somnambulist Cesare, who can purportedly predict the future of curious fairgoers. But at night, the doctor wakes Cesare from his sleep to enact his evil bidding… Incalculably influential, the film's nightmarishly jagged sets, sinister atmospheric and psychological emphasis left an immediate impact in its wake (horror, film noir, and gothic cinema would all be shaped directly by it).

title: MY NAME AIN’T SUZIE / FA GAI SI DOI
description: Positioned as a rebuke to the colonial fantasy of THE WORLD OF SUZIE WONG (1960), MY NAME AIN’T SUZIE spans three decades of the life of a girl from a poor fishing village who makes a name for herself as a courtesan in the Wan Chai red light district in Hong Kong. Over the course of the film, MY NAME AIN’T SUZIE confronts and redresses the occidental fantasies of the East through the protagonists’ interactions with her clients.

title: A Nightmare On Elm Street
description: In Wes Craven's classic slasher film, several Midwestern teenagers fall prey to Freddy Krueger (Robert Englund), a disfigured midnight mangler who preys on the teenagers in their dreams -- which, in turn, kills them in reality. After investigating the phenomenon, Nancy (Heather Langenkamp) begins to suspect that a dark secret kept by her and her friends' parents may be the key to unraveling the mystery, but can Nancy and her boyfriend Glen (Johnny Depp) solve the puzzle before it's too late?

title: COMBAT BREATHING: POSTSCRIPTS OF MODERNITY, PART 2: AMUSSU
description: The promises and outcomes of modernity – nation-states and capitalist economies, along with their alienating and extractivist logics and infrastructures – have produced immeasurable catastrophic damage to peoples and living environments across racial and class lines. Throughout their reign, these violent systems have not simply been justified by the values of universality, individual freedom, and liberal secular democracy; they have been produced through them, eliminating and exploiting all that does not measure up or conform to their suffocating parameters. Central to modernity, and to modern discourse more broadly, is the capture of technology as a transhistorical practice and its transformation into a supposedly modern conception governed by the logic of progress. “Postscripts of Modernity” is a film program that engages these catastrophic and violent legacies while demonstrating how film, itself a modern technology, might visualize and facilitate other social relations – in other words, how existing at-hand technologies, currently governed by the reign of capital, might be appropriated and subverted to achieve ends nonsynchronous with their intended uses. The works by Hong Kong Documentary Filmmakers, Bahar Noorizadeh, and Nadir Bouhmouch disavow modernity’s violence not by returning to an imagined precolonial or precapitalist past, but by insisting on a kind of crude presentism. Their diverse aesthetic interventions within the political contexts they respectively work in embrace whatever tools are currently available within modernity as material for the struggle against it. Nadir Bouhmouch AMUSSU 2019, 100 min, DCP The people of the Moroccan village of Imider may live alongside the largest silver mine in Africa, but they have reaped few of its benefits. The mine’s encroachment upon their communal life has rendered their existence increasingly precarious, contributing to water scarcity and threatening the community’s almond orchards, oasis, and traditional ways of life. In 2011, the villagers responded by shutting down a pipeline supplying water to the mine and establishing a protest camp around it, inaugurating a struggle that would last to this day. Rather than centering scenes of confrontation, arrest, intimidation, and police violence, which are all part of the fight against the infrastructures of this pipeline, AMUSSU turns its attention to the everyday life, resilience, and creativity of those who sustain the struggle. Conceived as a participatory filmic project, AMUSSU was produced through collective decision-making guided by the community’s Agraw protocol, while community members not only learned to operate film equipment but also participated directly in filming. In this sense, the film constitutes both a formal and methodological intervention into the practice of radical independent cinema. Years after the initial uprising, the protest camp has evolved into a small, largely self-sufficient community, where music, theater, poetry, and other artistic practices have emerged as a revolutionary vernacular. These forms of expression do more than accompany the struggle, as they become part of its infrastructure, sustaining collective memory, solidarity, and an ongoing demand for land, water, and a life lived with dignity. Introduced by Alma Chaouachi.

title: Szamanka
description: The screening on October 4th will be introduced by writer Daniel Bird. The screening on October 15th will be introduced by…

title: The Shining [UK Version]
description: Jack Torrance (Jack Nicholson) becomes winter caretaker at the isolated Overlook Hotel in Colorado, hoping to cure his writer's block. He settles in along with his wife, Wendy (Shelley Duvall), and his son, Danny (Danny Lloyd), who is plagued by psychic premonitions. As Jack's writing goes nowhere and Danny's visions become more disturbing, Jack discovers the hotel's dark secrets and begins to unravel into a homicidal maniac hell-bent on terrorizing his family.

title: Nadja • 4K Restoration
description: In 1993, invited by David Lynch to come up with a low-budget genre movie, Michael Almereyda (Tesla, Experimenter, Hamlet) came up with a moody, postmodern reimagining of the Dracula myth which draws inspiration from Dracula’s Daughter (1936) and André Breton’s surrealist novel Nadja. The film follows estranged vampire twins Nadja (Elina Löwensohn) and Edgar (a young Jared Harris) as they reunite following their father’s death by the flamboyantly unhinged Dr. Van Helsing, played with relish by Peter Fonda. The film’s striking visuals combine high-contrast black-and-white 35mm cinematography with the hallucinatory grain of Pixelvision video, looking better than ever in this new 4K restoration of the director’s cut. New 4K restoration of the director’s cut c/o Arbelos Films and Radiance Films.

title: SEDUCTION: THE CRUEL WOMAN
description: In SEDUCTION: THE CRUEL WOMAN, Wanda is a dominatrix and gallerist who invites patrons to witness her scenes with her submissives. Inspired by the Marquis de Sade’s “Venus in Furs”, writer-directors Monika Treut and Elfi Mikesch spin Sade’s tale of power, apathy, and pleasure to foreground the role the spectator (both imagined and real) plays in enabling these violating acts to occur.

title: Cruising
description: There’s a killer on the loose in New York City, and he’s targeting gay men in the West Village. Fortunately for the NYPD, he’s got a type – slim, dark-haired, handsome – and officer Steve Burns (Al Pacino) fits the bill. To crack the case, Steve must journey into the city’s nocturnal underworld of S&M and leather bars, hoping to catch the killer’s eye – but will he lose himself along the way? Controversial with both straight and gay audiences upon its initial release, Friedkin’s film still retains its power to shock and unsettle 45 years later.

title: The Howling
description: After a bizarre and near fatal encounter with a serial killer, a newswoman is sent to a rehabilitation center whose inhabitants may not be what they seem.

title: Wake in Fright - 4K Restoration
description: Theatrical English premiere of the new 4K Restoration, courtesy of Arrow Video. After finishing up the school term in a remote outback town, teacher John Grant (Gary Bond) looks forward to spending his holiday with his girlfriend in Sydney. But John gets waylaid in a mining town where a gambling spree leaves him completely broke. He quickly falls in with the hard-drinking locals, who constantly ply him with alcohol and force him to participate in a gruesome kangaroo hunt. Disgusted, John tries to hitchhike out of town and, when that fails, begins to contemplate suicide.

title: Underworld
description: Vampires and werewolves have waged a nocturnal war against each other for centuries. But all bets are off when a female vampire warrior named Selene, who's famous for her strength and werewolf-hunting prowess, becomes smitten with a peace-loving male werewolf, Michael, who wants to end the war.

title: The Thing
description: In remote Antarctica, a group of American research scientists are disturbed at their base camp by a helicopter shooting at a sled dog. When they take in the dog, it brutally attacks both human beings and canines in the camp and they discover that the beast can assume the shape of its victims. A resourceful helicopter pilot (Kurt Russell) and the camp doctor (Richard Dysart) lead the camp crew in a desperate, gory battle against the vicious creature before it picks them all off, one by one.

title: Teen Wolf
description: * ON SALE 21st SEPT * When a shy teenager’s newfound powers help him score at basketball - and with the popular girls - he has some pretty hairy decisions to make.

title: Our Land
description: OUR LAND dares to tread where few have trespassed before, asking the timely question of who has the right to roam in the English countryside? The UK is a wild and beautiful place, but the vast majority of it is off limits to the general public, with 92% of land and 97% of all rivers in England not legally accessible. At the same time, it is a landscape shaped by centuries of inheritance and tradition, with land held and cared for by families across multiple generations. OUR LAND takes us to the heart of the ‘Right to Roam’ movement as it embarks on a provocative trail of mass trespass, campaigning and education, while also exploring landowners’ concerns around environmental protection and the danger such widespread access could pose to a landscape already under threat.

title: MOMMY IS COMING
description: When the woes of monogamy affect the queer sex life of Dylan and Claudia, the couple enlist the help of sex professionals to reinvigorate their passion. These professionals range from the dominatrixes of the underground nightclub dungeons in Berlin to the sex educational help of Dylan’s mom. Through these sexcapades the women learn about their self-esteem, libido, and all the ways in which they become their mothers.

title: AFA MEMBERS ONLY: TWILIGHT ZONE ON 16MM
description: Anthology’s Members-Only screenings feature sneak-previews of upcoming features, programs of rare materials from Anthology’s collections, in-person filmmaker presentations, and more! The benefits of an Anthology membership have always been plentiful: free admission to over 100 Essential Cinema programs, reduced admission to all other shows, and discounted AFA publications. But with these screenings – free, open only to members, and including special receptions – we sweeten the pot even further. For the next Members-Only event, we’ll present two episodes of THE TWILIGHT ZONE – the classic TIME ENOUGH AT LAST and the timely, extreme-heat-themed THE MIDNIGHT SUN – screening from 16mm prints that reside in Anthology’s collection (thanks to a donation by David Mulkins). The screening will culminate with a special, unannounced film! Become a member at our box office, or at anthologyfilmarchives.org John Brahm TIME ENOUGH AT LAST 1959, 27 min, 16mm. Written by Rod Serling. With Burgess Meredith. Anton Leader THE MIDNIGHT SUN 1961, 27 min, 16mm. Written by Rod Serling. With Lois Nettleton. Plus, a special surprise! Total running time: ca. 85 min.

title: Boris Godunov
description: The screening on October 5th will be introduced by writer Daniel Bird. There will be a special screening of Boris Godunov on…

title: An American Werewolf in London
description: David (David Naughton) and Jack (Griffin Dunne), two American college students, are backpacking through Britain when a large wolf attacks them. David survives with a bite, but Jack is brutally killed. As David heals in the hospital, he's plagued by violent nightmares of his mutilated friend, who warns David that he is becoming a werewolf. When David discovers the horrible truth, he contemplates committing suicide before the next full moon causes him to transform from man to murderous beast.

title: ALANIS
description: Set in Argentina, ALANIS navigates the life of a single sex working parent. Though Alanis faces a deluge of problems with clients that plague every woman selling sex, the real threat to her security and the safety of her child stems from the social workers and laws that construct obstacles under the guise of protecting “precarious” women and children.

title: Trouble Every Day
description: Scientist Shane Brown (Vincent Gallo) neglects his new bride (Tricia Vessey), instead spending their honeymoon searching for an old colleague who disappeared after a research paper he had written was discredited by the medical community. It turns out that Dr. Semeneau is living in obscurity in order to protect his wife (Béatrice Dalle), whom he keeps prisoner in a room with boards nailed across the doorway. The narrative unfolds the dark secret that drives each party.

title: Hellraiser
description: Sexual deviant Frank (Sean Chapman) inadvertently opens a portal to hell when he tinkers with a box he bought while abroad. The act unleashes gruesome beings called Cenobites, who tear Frank's body apart. When Frank's brother (Andrew Robinson) and his wife, Julia (Clare Higgins), move into Frank's old house, they accidentally bring what is left of Frank back to life. Frank then convinces Julia, his one-time lover, to lure men back to the house so he can use their blood to reconstruct himself.

title: Manhunter : The Final Cut
description: A retired criminal profiler (William Petersen) reluctantly returns to the FBI to help track down a serial killer of families and is forced to consult an expert—the imprisoned Dr. Hannibal Lecktor (Brian Cox in a subtly chilling performance). The third feature written and directed by Michael Mann is a gripping adaptation of the first of Thomas Harris’s four novels featuring the iconic murderer, and benefits from the filmmaker’s typically striking visuals as well as a top-notch supporting cast , including Tom Noonan as the hunted killer, and three-time Oscar nominee Joan Allen (The Contender, 2000) as his blind love interest. -- This new 4K Final Cut, overseen by Mann, enhances the film’s depth, visual clarity and sound, offering audiences the ultimate immersive version. Shot in 1985, MANHUNTER was on a frontier in both its subject matter and film form, initiating an impressive list of subsequent films and series. “40 years ago – though armed with Thomas Harris’ excellent novel, “Red Dragon” – its subject matter, the profiling of serial killers, as well as being shocking and raw, was unknown. When adapting, I wanted to make its storytelling deliver audiences into a certain state of threat and emotional engagement. Integral to that was the visualization and use of music with lyrics sometimes working like a libretto. We have carefully remastered the film to try to evoke that mood and intensity, heightened with audio sourced from the original 5.1 35mm analog masters. This latest iteration is that version of the film with which I’m most satisfied.” said director Michael Mann. Under the guidance of Mann, this 4K scan of the original 35mm negative – with a few shots from an interpositive - was conformed and digitally restored at L’Immagine Ritrovata in Bologna. Both the theatrical version and the UHD HDR & SDR video color gradings were performed by Stefan Sonnenfeld at Company 3 in Los Angeles with the director. Sound restoration was done at Audio Mechanics from an original 35mm magnetic 6-track printmaster to release a new 5.1 mix by Luke Schwartzweller at Fox . Technical coordination and deliveries were managed by L’Immagine Ritrovata . This project was supervised by Becca Mann and STUDIOCANAL team, Jean-Pierre Boiget and Delphine Roussel . For Michael Mann, the process is about renewing the film’s immediacy for contemporary audiences: “If the picture was left the way it was, it would be interesting, but you’d feel some distance …you’d be observing it somewhat. I’m more interested in its original intent impacting you the same way it may have in 1986…that is, to bring you into it again in the original way.” As a film distinguished by its striking visual style, including Colleen Attwood’s costume design, Academy Award- winner Mel Bourne’s art direction, Dante Spinotti’s lighting, Mann worked with his long-time collaborator, Stefan Sonnenfeld (Company 3), to develop a new color grade for ‘The Final Cut’ that engages a contemporary audience while honoring the film’s lasting legacy. “A good example is the use of primaries and secondaries in combinations that don’t occur in nature for an unsettling ambiance or the use of blue for night-time imagery. We’ve changed values subtly sometimes, but significantly, to enhance the impact without changing the dramatic intent of the film,” said Stefan Sonnenfeld. He adds: “Michael… wants you to understand the story and the mood and the environment… and then asks you to interpret that in colour… He also tells you what emotion he’s trying to evoke from the scene.” The new version also introduces an HDR presentation, offering an intensified new experience. “So that nobody’s ever seen the movie like that,” noted Sonnenfeld.

title: Possession
description: After Anna (Isabelle Adjani) reveals to her husband, Mark (Sam Neill), that she is having an affair, she leaves him and their son. Mark is devastated, and seeks out Heinrich (Heinz Bennent), the man who cuckolded him, only to receive a beating. After a series of violent confrontations between Mark and Anna, Mark hires a private investigator to follow her. Anna descends into madness, and it's soon clear that she is hiding a much bigger secret -- one that is both inexplicable and shocking.

title: The Silence of the Lambs
description: Jodie Foster stars as Clarice Starling, a top student at the FBI's training academy. Jack Crawford (Scott Glenn) wants Clarice to interview Dr. Hannibal Lecter (Anthony Hopkins), a brilliant psychiatrist who is also a violent psychopath, serving life behind bars for various acts of murder and cannibalism. Crawford believes that Lecter may have insight into a case and that Starling, as an attractive young woman, may be just the bait to draw him out.

title: Obsession (2026)
description: After breaking the mysterious "One Wish Willow" to win his crush's heart, a hopeless romantic finds himself getting exactly what he asked for but soon discovers that some desires come at a dark, sinister price.

title: The Ear
description: Our screening on Tuesday 6 October will be introduced Daniela Richterová, Senior Lecturer in Intelligence Studies at the Department of War…

title: Irreversible
description: A woman's lover and her ex-boyfriend take justice into their own hands after she becomes the victim of a rapist. Because some acts can't be undone. Because man is an animal. Because the desire for vengeance is a natural impulse. Because most crimes remain unpunished.

title: COMBAT BREATHING: LABORING IMAGES, PART 1
description: LABORING IMAGES, IMAGING LABOR, PART 1 In 1895, cinema’s inaugural image was made by Louis Lumière in France. Autologically titled LA SORTIE DE L’USINE LUMIÈRE À LYON (WORKERS LEAVING THE LUMIÈRE FACTORY IN LYON), the silent black-and-white film holds its frame still as workers exit the factory gates. Replete with historical and symbolic connotations, this early image – revisited and reexamined by Harun Farocki nearly a century later – both refers to cinematic technology’s inextricable relationship with emergent forms of modern industrial labor while it simultaneously stages the factory floor, long imagined as labor’s primary site of exploitation and organization, as being left behind. “Laboring Images, Imaging Labor” departs from this visually rendered tension by considering how labor constitutes film and how film, in turn, gives form to structurally occluded and socially dispersed realities and conditions of labor. Moving from reflections on the position of labor under communist social formations; to the uncounted, feminized work of social reproduction; to the psychic and gestural labors of revolutionary dreaming and fugitive plotting; to the co-constitutive relationships between racialization and ascendant regimes of gig and AI-training labor, the films gathered here ask what makes – and unmakes – the laboring social body and the formations it sustains. The works of Sara Gómez, Dina Mimi, Maissa Maatouk, Nicolas Gourault, and Jean-Marie Straub and Danièle Huillet show us not only what comprises the systemic category of labor under global capitalism, but how moving images make labor’s multiple, stratified realities perceptible. Sara Gómez ABOUT EXTRA HOURS AND VOLUNTEER WORK / SOBRE HORAS EXTRAS Y TRABAJO VOLUNTARIO (1973, 9 min, 16mm-to-DCP) At the 1973 congress of the Confederation of Cuban Workers, textile workers debate the value and necessity of unpaid overtime and “voluntary work” within the country’s economic development plans. Sara Gómez edits their testimonies against voice-over, intertitles, and images of Fidel Castro, Che Guevara, and Ho Chi Minh working alongside laborers. Revolutionary rhetoric fills the screen as workers describe unnecessary overtime, administrative disorder, and tasks performed for their symbolic rather than practical value. One woman recalls being sent three times to move the same stones, each time to a different place. Neither a rejection of collective labor nor an affirmation of its official representation, EXTRA HOURS AND VOLUNTARY WORK asks what voluntarism means when organized through institutional pressure, and whether labor undertaken in the name of revolution can remain emancipatory when workers have little power over its purpose or conditions. Sara Gómez YEAR ONE / AÑO UNO (1972, 9 min, 16mm-to-DCP) In YEAR ONE, Sara Gómez turns to the period immediately after childbirth, foregrounding the care and material support required of new mothers. Postnatal care emerges not as a private concern or a given resource but as a collective responsibility, bringing the intimate labor of feeding, healing, and sustaining life into the political field of revolutionary transformation. By attending to forms of work historically naturalized as feminine – and therefore rendered invisible or unremunerated – the film considers how women’s emancipation depends upon a reorganization of everyday life. Gómez locates the revolution not only in the transformation of economic production but also in the institutions, social relations, and infrastructures through which life is reproduced. YEAR ONE asks what forms of collective provision might relieve women of the unequal burdens of care, and what a revolution must make possible for those whose bodies and labor sustain its future. Dina Mimi THOUSAND THRASHING ARMS (2024, 13 min, DCP) Frantz Fanon famously observed that “the first thing which the native learns is to stay in his place, and not to go beyond certain limits.” Against the enforced stillness of colonial order, the native dreams of “jumping, swimming, running, climbing.” Drawing on Fanon’s account of the colonized body and its fugitive dream life, THOUSAND THRASHING ARMS examines the relationship between liberation struggle, dreaming, and movement. Through an elusive montage of statues, animals, and bodies wrapped in cloth, the film traces figures held captive, traversing tunnels, resisting underground, or struggling to emerge. The body appears as an instrument of control, a site of resistance, and a vessel of rebellion, while movement becomes double-edged – both disciplined and made productive – exceeding the limits imposed upon it. The image of labor performed, pixelated, stretched, and overlayered, is material, political, and oneiric – the labor of dreaming and revolting, rehearsing in sleep what the waking body is forbidden to do; what it will one day do during wakeful hours. Maissa Maatouk EXERCISE IN WAITING, (2023, 7 min, DCP) In the wake of Lebanon’s 2019 economic collapse, Beirut witnessed the rapid expansion of the gig economy and digital labor platforms that drew surplus labor into new circuits of capitalist valorization. EXERCISE IN WAITING follows migrant service workers managed through the city’s dominant delivery app in 2023, which mediates among customers, restaurants and shops, and couriers. Set in Beirut’s Manara neighborhood, the film observes the vacant lots where couriers gather to rest between deliveries. With minimal poetic intervention, it dwells on the uneasy temporality of waiting and the restless immanence registered in the workers’ gestures as they oscillate between agitation and stillness. Always passing through or pausing between orders, the men rest amid seemingly impervious yellow chamomile flowers. Nicolas Gourault THEIR EYES (2025, 23 min, DCP) How does a machine learn to read the world? THEIR EYES follows online microworkers in the Global South whose task is to train the artificial intelligence used by self-driving cars in the Global North. Through testimonies and screen recordings, the film attends to the workers’ encounters with images of U.S. streets: identifying objects, interpreting movements, and translating visual ambiguity into data. Yet these acts of looking are not entirely contained by the task. As workers reflect on the distant worlds passing across their screens, they devise small ways of organizing, withholding, and interfering with the system that coordinates their labor. The film considers how geographically dispersed workers are made to inhabit the machine’s vision – and how their own forms of attention might exceed it. Total running time: ca. 65 min. Introduced by Nour Annan.

title: MOMMY IS COMING
description: When the woes of monogamy affect the queer sex life of Dylan and Claudia, the couple enlist the help of sex professionals to reinvigorate their passion. These professionals range from the dominatrixes of the underground nightclub dungeons in Berlin to the sex educational help of Dylan’s mom. Through these sexcapades the women learn about their self-esteem, libido, and all the ways in which they become their mothers.

title: COMBAT BREATHING: LABORING IMAGES, PART 2: SICILIA!
description: LABORING IMAGES, IMAGING LABOR, PART 2 In 1895, cinema’s inaugural image was made by Louis Lumière in France. Autologically titled LA SORTIE DE L’USINE LUMIÈRE À LYON (WORKERS LEAVING THE LUMIÈRE FACTORY IN LYON), the silent black-and-white film holds its frame still as workers exit the factory gates. Moving from reflections on the position of labor under communist social formations; to the uncounted, feminized work of social reproduction; to the psychic and gestural labors of revolutionary dreaming and fugitive plotting; to the co-constitutive relationships between racialization and ascendant regimes of gig and AI-training labor, the films gathered here ask what makes – and unmakes – the laboring social body and the formations it sustains. The works of Sara Gómez, Dina Mimi, Maissa Maatouk, Nicolas Gourault, and Jean-Marie Straub and Danièle Huillet show us not only what comprises the systemic category of labor under global capitalism, but how moving images make labor’s multiple, stratified realities perceptible. Jean-Marie Straub & Danièle Huillet SICILIA! 1999, 66 min, 35mm Adapted from Elio Vittorini’s antifascist novel “Conversations in Sicily”, Straub and Huillet’s SICILIA! follows Silvestro, a migrant returning to his native island after fifteen years in New York to visit his mother. Silvestro’s journey unfolds through a series of encounters: with an orange seller unable to live from his crop, fellow passengers, and a knife grinder searching for blades to sharpen. Their highly composed conversations move between hunger, unemployment, migration, socialism, and the dignity of an honest day’s work. The return home offers neither restoration nor escape; instead, it reveals how displacement binds distant geographies through shared conditions of dispossession. Straub and Huillet locate antifascism within speech, memory, and the gestures of working people, whose experiences resist the language imposed upon them by the state. In the film’s stark images and carefully measured voices, labor becomes both a record of exploitation and a living repository of the substance necessary for revolution.

title: KAMA SUTRA: A TALE OF LOVE
description: In KAMA SUTRA: A TALE OF LOVE, Mira Nair examines the stigmatization of sexually promiscuous and unmarried women by the upper class in 16th-century India. The film follows Maya, a servant, who embarks on a journey of self-discovery through the art and spiritual practice of being a courtesan. Though ultimately a film about love, as signaled in the title, the film presents a rare historical fictional account of the spiritual art of working sex in the 16th-century.

title: The Exorcist (Extended Cut)
description: One of the most profitable horror movies ever made, this tale of an exorcism is based loosely on actual events. When young Regan (Linda Blair) starts acting odd -- levitating, speaking in tongues -- her worried mother (Ellen Burstyn) seeks medical help, only to hit a dead end. A local priest (Jason Miller), however, thinks the girl may be seized by the devil. The priest makes a request to perform an exorcism, and the church sends in an expert (Max von Sydow) to help with the difficult job.

title: Blacula
description: During a visit to Transylvania, an African prince (William Marshall) gets turned into a vampire by Count Dracula (Charles Macaulay). Sealed in a coffin for several lifetimes, "Blacula" reawakens in 1970s Los Angeles. Leaving a trail of bloodless victims in his wake, he pursues Lina (Vonetta McGee), a woman who bears a striking resemblance to his dead wife. Meanwhile, Dr. Gordon Thomas (Thalmus Rasulala) and top cop Lt. Peters (Gordon Pinsent) are hot on the bloodsucker's trail.

title: Halloween III: Season of the Witch
description: After a terrified toy salesman is mysteriously attacked and brought to the hospital clutching the year's most popular Halloween mask, Dr. Daniel Challis sets out to investigate the strange events and finds himself thrust into a nightmarish conspiracy.

title: The Thing
description: In remote Antarctica, a group of American research scientists are disturbed at their base camp by a helicopter shooting at a sled dog. When they take in the dog, it brutally attacks both human beings and canines in the camp and they discover that the beast can assume the shape of its victims. A resourceful helicopter pilot (Kurt Russell) and the camp doctor (Richard Dysart) lead the camp crew in a desperate, gory battle against the vicious creature before it picks them all off, one by one.

title: The Shining [UK Version]
description: Jack Torrance (Jack Nicholson) becomes winter caretaker at the isolated Overlook Hotel in Colorado, hoping to cure his writer's block. He settles in along with his wife, Wendy (Shelley Duvall), and his son, Danny (Danny Lloyd), who is plagued by psychic premonitions. As Jack's writing goes nowhere and Danny's visions become more disturbing, Jack discovers the hotel's dark secrets and begins to unravel into a homicidal maniac hell-bent on terrorizing his family.

title: Child's Play (1988)
description: When serial killer Charles Lee Ray (Brad Dourif) is mortally wounded in a police shoot-out, he uses a voodoo spell to transfer his soul into Chucky, an innocuous ‘Good Guys' doll. Young Andy (Alex Vincent) receives him as a birthday gift, and Chucky soon embarks on a killing spree. However, Charles doesn't want to be trapped in the body of the doll forever; escape is possible by transferring his personality into the first human he reveals his identity to... and naturally Andy is curious about his new toy.

title: Mystery Horror Movie
description: HorrOctober invades our Mystery Movie strand this October! We'll be serving up four Mystery Horror Movies over four weeks! That is the only hint we will give you! No other hints. No clues. No refunds! You can find a list of every MYSTERY MOVIE we have ever screened HERE ; if a film is on this list, it is not eligible for future Mystery Movie screenings! --- Content Advice : As these films are a mystery, we aren't able to provide specific ratings / guidance on the film's content. We strongly advise that you take this into consideration before purchasing a ticket.

title: Critical Affection Trilogy by Michelle Williams Gamaker (15)
MY NAME AIN’T SUZIE / FA GAI SI DOI
description: Positioned as a rebuke to the colonial fantasy of THE WORLD OF SUZIE WONG (1960), MY NAME AIN’T SUZIE spans three decades of the life of a girl from a poor fishing village who makes a name for herself as a courtesan in the Wan Chai red light district in Hong Kong. Over the course of the film, MY NAME AIN’T SUZIE confronts and redresses the occidental fantasies of the East through the protagonists’ interactions with her clients.

title: THE SECRET LIFE OF…ANTHOLOGY FILM ARCHIVES
description: We continue our longstanding tradition of presenting “The Secret Life of…Anthology Film Archives”, a recurring opportunity to take a peek at the teeming hive of creativity hiding behind the scenes at Anthology, thanks to the film- and video-making efforts of AFA’s staff, friends, fellow-travelers, and devotees.

title: SEDUCTION: THE CRUEL WOMAN
description: In SEDUCTION: THE CRUEL WOMAN, Wanda is a dominatrix and gallerist who invites patrons to witness her scenes with her submissives. Inspired by the Marquis de Sade’s “Venus in Furs”, writer-directors Monika Treut and Elfi Mikesch spin Sade’s tale of power, apathy, and pleasure to foreground the role the spectator (both imagined and real) plays in enabling these violating acts to occur.

title: Suspiria [1977]
description: Suzy (Jessica Harper) travels to Germany to attend ballet school. When she arrives, late on a stormy night, no one lets her in, and she sees Pat (Eva Axén), another student, fleeing from the school. When Pat reaches her apartment, she is murdered. The next day, Suzy is admitted to her new school, but has a difficult time settling in. She hears noises, and often feels ill. As more people die, Suzy uncovers the terrifying secret history of the place.

title: In The Mood For Love
description: In 1962 Hong Kong, neighbors Su Li-zhen (Mrs. Chan) and Chow Mo-wan (Mr. Chow) discover their spouses are having an affair. As they spend time together, they develop feelings for each other, but their relationship remains chaste and unspoken, reflecting societal constraints and their own moral compass.

title: Zombie Flesh Eaters [Zombi 2]
description: After an abandoned boat sails into New York harbor with a zombie aboard, a reporter teams up with the daughter of the boat's missing captain to investigate the island where he was last seen conducting research—the site of an alleged zombie outbreak.

title: Nostalgia [Nostalghia]
description: Andrei Tarkovsky’s unforgettably haunting film, his first to be made outside Russia, explores the melancholy of the expatriate through the film’s protagonist, Gorchakov, a Russian poet researching in Italy. Arriving at a Tuscan village spa with Eugenia, his beautiful Italian interpreter, Gorchakov is visited by memories of Russia and of his wife and children, and he encounters the local mystic who sets him a challenging task. ‘Nostalgia’ is filled with a series of mysterious and extraordinary images, all of which coalesce into a miraculous whole in the film’s final shot. As in all Tarkovsky’s films, nature, the elements of fire and water, music, painting and poetry all play a major role. ★★★★ “Hauntingly beautiful” - David Parkinson, Empire

title: Cinema Paradiso [Nuovo Cinema Paradiso]
description: A winner of awards across the world including Best Foreign Language Film Oscar, 5 BAFTA Awards including Best Actor, Original Screenplay and Score, the Grand Prize of the Jury at the Cannes Film Festival and many more. Giuseppe Tornatore's loving homage to the cinema tells the story of Salvatore, a successful film director, returning home for the funeral of Alfredo, his old friend who was the projectionist at the local cinema throughout his childhood. Soon memories of his first love affair with the beautiful Elena and all the highs and lows that shaped his life come flooding back, as Salvatore reconnects with the community he left 30 years earlier.

title: House of 1000 Corpses
description: Two young couples traveling across the backwoods of Texas searching for urban legends of murder end up as prisoners of a bizarre and sadistic backwater family of serial killers.
