title: COMBAT BREATHING: READ MY DESIRE, PART 1
description: READ MY DESIRE, PART 1 Social orders are resisted and overturned not merely because the dominant classes create unlivable conditions for the dominated classes, but also because the dominated classes actively and transgenerationally imagine, prefigure, and desire the realization of alternative social relations that cannot be accommodated by the present order. Such disruptive, exorbitant, and irrepressible desires – often structurally designated as queer – are the focus of this program. “Read My Desire” invokes the work of philosopher Joan Copjec and echoes her formulations that desire precisely emerges from the divisions within the subject which cannot be reduced to social identity or captured by historical regimes. Bringing together historical and contemporary works to explore cinema’s desire-producing capacity as well as the often-elided place of desire, love, eroticism, and sensuality in social movements and associated streams of cultural production, the program traverses multiple geographies and genres, including sci-fi, music video, mythical fable, narrative drama, parodic documentary, and experimental film. The selected works by Marlon Riggs, Valentin Noujaïm, Michelle Parkerson, Peng Zuqiang, Jumana Manna, and Naomi Rincon Gallardo theorize the function of desire in reorienting the horizons of liberation struggles and affirming subjectivities at continual risk of erasure. Marlon Riggs ANTHEM 1991, 9 min, DCP “Every time we kiss we confirm the new world coming.” This is one among many of the defiant phrases voiced in Marlon Riggs’s experimental and agitational music video, which politicizes black male homoeroticism through its African rhythm-informed combination of socially charged images, symbols, dance, text, and spoken poetry. Produced during an era marked by state-backed cultural repression, neoliberalization, and an escalating HIV epidemic, Riggs’s audiovisual manifesto calls on its viewers to “pervert the language” – an act it reflexively performs through its appropriation of a popular and desire-inducing commercial form for the ends of black queer revolution. Valentin Noujaïm OCEANIA 2024, 24 min, 16mm-to-DCP Set in the apartment complex of a quiet French suburb, Valentin Noujaïm’s short film revolves around the entwined personal and socio-political yearnings of its teenage diasporic protagonist, Najib. Upon learning of the passing of an elderly Algerian neighbor from his mother, Najib takes the keys to the deceased man’s apartment only to discover a world of unanswered questions, from letters penned by a former lover to archival videos of pan-African cultural festivals, and other ephemera. An ode to the often-unconscious drives of desire, OCEANIA gestures toward the oblique modes by which past struggles are continually carried on but also transformed by newer generations. Michelle Parkerson ODDS AND ENDS 1993, 28 min, DCP ODDS AND ENDS is a pioneering work of science fiction that capaciously mobilizes the speculative dimensions of the genre to center black lesbian militancy and futurity. The campy intergalactic fable unfolds in the year 2096 – by way of striking allegorical correspondences with the conditions of the fascistic present – in which a cast of black women warriors wage a battle against “ultra-right-wing clones” who seek their annihilation. Michelle Parkerson’s new-age short uncovers psychic and fleshly sites of desire and sexuality within revolutionary movements through its lead character, Lieutenant Loz Wayard, a courageous young amazon, who learns the price of passion when her beloved Sephra takes on the ultimate sacrifice for the struggle. Total running time: ca. 65 min. Introduced by Carlos Motta.

title: VIKA KIRCHENBAUER PGM 1
description: We enter this program with a salacious direct address-cum-invitation in PLEASE RELAX NOW, as Kirchenbauer seduces the viewer from a black box void, stretching the edges of imagination. In LIKE RATS LEAVING A SINKING SHIP, Kirchenbauer layers psychiatric assessments to consider the coherency of a biography, and assess the ways in which individual memory is puppeted by state apparatuses. Both SHE WHOSE BLOOD IS CLOTTING IN MY UNDERWEAR and MOOD MANAGEMENT again push the viewer’s capacity to render a coherent picture of actions, generating a half-constructed image which lends itself only then to a projection. Both works are guided by Kirchenbauer’s music project, COOL FOR YOU. Through essay and material vignettes, UNTITLED SEQUENCE OF GAPS explores light outside of the visible spectrum to consider violence as it attaches to different kinds of visibility and invisibility. To tickle is a form of touch, an intimate act carried out to delight, to excite, or to torment. In THE ISLAND OF PERPETUAL TICKLING (III), Kirchenbauer surrenders to this metaphoric and literal tickle. Noting that it is impossible to tickle oneself, her task requires assistance. PLEASE RELAX NOW (2014, 12 min, DCP) LIKE RATS LEAVING A SINKING SHIP (2012, 24.5 min, DCP) SHE WHOSE BLOOD IS CLOTTING IN MY UNDERWEAR (2016, 3.5 min, DCP) MOOD MANAGEMENT 2017, 2 min, DCPUNTITLED SEQUENCE OF GAPS (2020, 12.5 min, DCP) THE ISLAND OF PERPETUAL TICKLING (III) (2018, 13 min, DCP) Total running time: ca. 75 min. Filmmaker Vika Kirchenbauer in person for both screenings!

title: COMBAT BREATHING: READ MY DESIRE, PART 2
description: READ MY DESIRE, PART 2 Social orders are resisted and overturned not merely because the dominant classes create unlivable conditions for the dominated classes, but also because the dominated classes actively and transgenerationally imagine, prefigure, and desire the realization of alternative social relations that cannot be accommodated by the present order. Such disruptive, exorbitant, and irrepressible desires – often structurally designated as queer – are the focus of this program. “Read My Desire” invokes the work of philosopher Joan Copjec and echoes her formulations that desire precisely emerges from the divisions within the subject which cannot be reduced to social identity or captured by historical regimes. Bringing together historical and contemporary works to explore cinema’s desire-producing capacity as well as the often-elided place of desire, love, eroticism, and sensuality in social movements and associated streams of cultural production, the program traverses multiple geographies and genres, including sci-fi, music video, mythical fable, narrative drama, parodic documentary, and experimental film. The selected works by Marlon Riggs, Valentin Noujaïm, Michelle Parkerson, Peng Zuqiang, Jumana Manna, and Naomi Rincon Gallardo theorize the function of desire in reorienting the horizons of liberation struggles and affirming subjectivities at continual risk of erasure. Peng Zuqiang SIGHT LEAK 2022, 12 min, 16mm & Super-8mm-to-DCP Peng Zuqiang’s SIGHT LEAK takes as its departure point Roland Barthes’s visit to China in 1973, using the French theorist’s published travel notes and his renowned writing on love and desire as source texts for exploring the objective and subjective machinations of class and looking. Shot on black-and-white film, SIGHT LEAK brims with minimal haptic images, from framed close-ups of body parts to natural and urban landscapes sensuously sculpted by plays of light and shadow. In the film, Peng’s camera trails behind a local tourist who travels through different spaces and gatherings, seemingly never looking at anyone, yet always silently looking at someone. Counterposing foreign and local projections – whether they be filmic, ideological, or psychic – SIGHT LEAK subtly alludes to the problematics of homoerotic imperial (mis)recognition while holding out the possibility for desire to produce non-normative, subterranean collectivities. Jumana Manna BLESSED BLESSED OBLIVION 2010, 21 min, DCP This early work by Jumana Manna offers a portrait of masculine performativity in East Jerusalem, as manifested in gyms, body shops, and hairdressing parlors. Inspired by Kenneth Anger’s SCORPIO RISING (1963), the video employs visual collage and a dynamic musical soundtrack as ironic commentary. Anger’s depiction of leather-clad bikers serves as a counterpoint to the social scene Manna portrays in BLESSED BLESSED OBLIVION, that of stereotyped male “thug” culture in Palestine. Close-up fragments construct an eroticized and parodic montage of bodies, cars, and locations, intersected by snippets of often-humorous dialogue and a monologue about the art of a car wash. Psychologizing the characters while also being seduced by them, Manna’s conflicted desires mirror those of her male protagonist who drifts from abject rants to declamations of heroic poetry and unashamed self-praise. Naomi Rincon Gallardo PATLACHE ANT NEST 2025, 21 min, DCP PATLACHE ANT NEST, the latest work by Naomi Rincon Gallardo, is a fable inspired by the image and description of an ambiguous figure called Patlache who appears in the Florentine Codex, a sixteenth-century colonial ethnographic research document about Mesoamerica created by a Spanish missionary priest. The Patlache was described in racially coded and gender disruptive terms – as a filthy woman with a penis and body hair who practices lesbian love. Merging camp DIY aesthetics and surreal, indigenous forms of storytelling, Gallardo mythically rearticulates the archival capture of this figure in PATLACHE ANT NEST with a cast of costumed characters representing toothed vaginas, leafcutter ants, and a cactus. Over the course of the film, the Patlache character transforms into a dome-like architectural structure bearing an entrance that leads to an underground, patriarchy-free dwelling of lesbian sociality and flourishing. Total running time: ca. 60 min. Introduced by Omar Alsayyed.

title: The Devil's Rejects
description: The murderous, backwoods Firefly family take to the road to escape the vengeful Sheriff Wydell, who is not afraid of being as ruthless as his target.

title: The Exorcist (Extended Cut)
description: One of the most profitable horror movies ever made, this tale of an exorcism is based loosely on actual events. When young Regan (Linda Blair) starts acting odd -- levitating, speaking in tongues -- her worried mother (Ellen Burstyn) seeks medical help, only to hit a dead end. A local priest (Jason Miller), however, thinks the girl may be seized by the devil. The priest makes a request to perform an exorcism, and the church sends in an expert (Max von Sydow) to help with the difficult job.

title: Don't Look Now
description: After the death of their child, a couple moves to Venice, where the husband has an assignment of restoring a church. There, they meet a sister who claims their kid is trying to warn them of a danger.

title: The Shining [UK Version]
description: Jack Torrance (Jack Nicholson) becomes winter caretaker at the isolated Overlook Hotel in Colorado, hoping to cure his writer's block. He settles in along with his wife, Wendy (Shelley Duvall), and his son, Danny (Danny Lloyd), who is plagued by psychic premonitions. As Jack's writing goes nowhere and Danny's visions become more disturbing, Jack discovers the hotel's dark secrets and begins to unravel into a homicidal maniac hell-bent on terrorizing his family.

title: The Craft
description: After transferring to a Los Angeles high school, Sarah (Robin Tunney) finds that her telekinetic gift appeals to a group of three wannabe witches, who happen to be seeking a fourth member for their rituals. Bonnie (Neve Campbell), Rochelle (Rachel True) and Nancy (Fairuza Balk), like Sarah herself, all have troubled backgrounds, which combined with their nascent powers lead to dangerous consequences. When a minor spell causes a fellow student to lose her hair, the girls grow power-mad.

title: A Nightmare On Elm Street
description: In Wes Craven's classic slasher film, several Midwestern teenagers fall prey to Freddy Krueger (Robert Englund), a disfigured midnight mangler who preys on the teenagers in their dreams -- which, in turn, kills them in reality. After investigating the phenomenon, Nancy (Heather Langenkamp) begins to suspect that a dark secret kept by her and her friends' parents may be the key to unraveling the mystery, but can Nancy and her boyfriend Glen (Johnny Depp) solve the puzzle before it's too late?

title: Dead Ringers
description: This screening will be introduced by Video Bazaar. In one of Cronenberg’s most renowned and psychologically intense thrillers, twin brothers switch…

title: VACANCES
description: FILMMAKER IN PERSON! A strange and unusual mixture of warts-and-all family portraiture, subtle exposé of class and privilege, and minimalist depiction of a particular setting that’s rendered with an almost miraculously tactile sense of presence, photographer and filmmaker Victoria Hely-Hutchinson’s VACANCES is a deceptively unassuming film. Filmed over the course of a decade at the property in Provence inhabited by Hely-Hutchinson’s outrageously uninhibited grandmother, a bohemian Austro-Hungarian countess and family matriarch, VACANCES grew out of Hely-Hutchinson’s 2016 short film of the same name, and is something of a filmic complement to her autobiographical 2023 book, “I Left My Grandmother’s House”. The documentary delves, with a grace and open-endedness that belies its analytical bite, into both the bigger-than-life personality of “granny” as well as the sometimes strained dynamics among the rest of the family, including Hely-Hutchinson’s grandfather, mother, and siblings. Unique in suggesting by turns cinema vérité, reality TV, chamber theater, and the minimalism of landscape cinema, VACANCES is a profoundly singular work – a film whose technique is nearly invisible, but which sneaks up on you with its trenchant perceptions, layered meanings, and emotional and filmic complexity. “This time-lapse film, shot over a period of ten years, follows members of several generations of a wealthy aristocratic family with Austro-Hungarian roots. The entire film is set in a Provençal villa, whose social heart is the swimming pool, around which the women gather to exchange various observations and, surreptitiously, gossip. The center of the family is the aging matriarch, who likes to talk about her extravagant, promiscuous life, but at the same time commands all the attention and authority of those around her. However, her influence gradually weakens with each passing generation.” –JI.HLAVA INTERNATIONAL DOCUMENTARY FILM FESTIVAL

title: VIKA KIRCHENBAUER PGM 2
description: In the second program of our 2-part retrospective devoted to Vika Kirchenbauer, we dive deeper into the politics of labor in contemporary art, as the artist offers us a WELCOME ADDRESS, directly calling into question the art economy’s coded-progressive positioning of difference and diversity as symbolic cultural currency. Considering the foul, late-stage capitalist “Experience Economy,” YOU ARE BORING troubles the nature of looking. THE CAPACITY FOR ADEQUATE ANGER positions still images from the artist’s presumable childhood archive, gaps of nothingness, and the essay form to offer a critique of the production of contemporary art in the face of upward mobility, mapping subjectivity and political agency. To close this program with a thorough and considered look at the complicit role of artists and art institutions, COMPASSION AND INCONVENIENCE takes us back to 18th century London to trace the first public exhibitions of contemporary art, when materiality intersects with ideology via Liberalism and Enlightenment, taking to task the economic and colonial interests that define/d the “pursuit of refinement.” WELCOME ADDRESS (2017, 9 min, DCP) YOU ARE BORING! (2015, 14 min, DCP) THE CAPACITY FOR ADEQUATE ANGER (2021, 15 min, DCP) COMPASSION AND INCONVENIENCE (2024, 30 min, DCP) Total running time: ca. 75 min. Filmmaker Vika Kirchenbauer in person for both screenings!

title: Psycho
description: Phoenix secretary Marion Crane (Janet Leigh), on the lam after stealing $40,000 from her employer in order to run away with her boyfriend, Sam Loomis (John Gavin), is overcome by exhaustion during a heavy rainstorm. Traveling on the back roads to avoid the police, she stops for the night at the ramshackle Bates Motel and meets the polite but highly strung proprietor Norman Bates (Anthony Perkins), a young man with an interest in taxidermy and a difficult relationship with his mother.

title: Halloween III: Season of the Witch
description: After a terrified toy salesman is mysteriously attacked and brought to the hospital clutching the year's most popular Halloween mask, Dr. Daniel Challis sets out to investigate the strange events and finds himself thrust into a nightmarish conspiracy.

description: Revisit the landmark of Asian Extreme Cinema, with an introduction by lead actor Tatsuya Fujiwara.

description: The film will be introduced by writer and historian Susan Jonusas on the 18th of September and by writer Stephen Thrower…

title: Possession
description: After Anna (Isabelle Adjani) reveals to her husband, Mark (Sam Neill), that she is having an affair, she leaves him and their son. Mark is devastated, and seeks out Heinrich (Heinz Bennent), the man who cuckolded him, only to receive a beating. After a series of violent confrontations between Mark and Anna, Mark hires a private investigator to follow her. Anna descends into madness, and it's soon clear that she is hiding a much bigger secret -- one that is both inexplicable and shocking.

title: PLAYING WITH FIRE: AN ECOSEXUAL EMERGENCY
description: Following their two previous films – GOODBYE GAULEY MOUNTAIN: AN ECOSEXUAL LOVE STORY (2014) and WATER MAKES US WET: AN ECOSEXUAL ADVENTURE (2019) – Annie Sprinkle and Beth Stephens bring us the third chapter in their climate crisis trilogy: PLAYING WITH FIRE: AN ECOSEXUAL EMERGENCY. With the climate crisis worsening with each passing season, the artist/activist duo sound the alarm by enlisting a collective of artists, elders, witches, neighbors, and friends, to examine the ways we can support the health of our dear Earth. Partially narrated by Boulder Creek’s mythical white peacock Albert and culminating in a ceremonial Wedding to Fire in the Redwoods, PLAYING WITH FIRE is a powerful portrait of queer resilience but also a reckoning with the power of fire, with its capacity to heal and its potential to destroy. Co-sponsored by Climate Film Festival and Queer New York International Arts Festival. Annie Sprinkle & Beth Stephens will be here in person for both screenings, and will present a ten-minute performative introduction before each show, “Ecosex 101”! On Saturday, Sprinkle & Stephens will appear for a post-screening discussion and Q&A led by Barbara Carellas, author of “The Book of Ecstasy”, and on Sunday, Angelo Madsen (director of A BODY TO LIVE IN) will lead a Q&A. Viewers are encouraged to dress up in the themes of fire and ecosex. After the Saturday screening, all are welcome to join a reception in the lobby. Beth and Annie will honor two legends of golden age adult entertainment and the co-founders of the first pornstar support group, Club 90. Veronica Vera is turning 80 and Veronica Hart is turning 70. Birthday cake will be served, and signed books and merch will be available for purchase.

title: The Red Shoes
description: In this classic drama, Vicky Page (Moira Shearer) is an aspiring ballerina torn between her dedication to dance and her desire to love. While her imperious instructor, Boris Lermontov (Anton Walbrook), urges to her to forget anything but ballet, Vicky begins to fall for the charming young composer Julian Craster (Marius Goring). Eventually Vicky, under great emotional stress, must choose to pursue either her art or her romance, a decision that carries serious consequences.

Co-sponsored by Climate Film Festival and Queer New York International Arts Festival. Annie Sprinkle & Beth Stephens will be here in person for both screenings, and will present a ten-minute performative introduction before each show, “Ecosex 101”! On Saturday, Sprinkle & Stephens will appear for a post-screening discussion and Q&A led by Barbara Carellas, author of “The Book of Ecstasy”, and on Sunday, Angelo Madsen (director of A BODY TO LIVE IN) will lead a Q&A. Viewers are encouraged to dress up in the themes of fire and ecosex. After the Saturday screening, all are welcome to join a reception in the lobby. Beth and Annie will honor two legends of golden age adult entertainment and the co-founders of the first pornstar support group, Club 90. Veronica Vera is turning 80 and Veronica Hart is turning 70. Birthday cake will be served, and signed books and merch will be available for purchase.

title: VACANCES
description: FILMMAKER IN PERSON! A strange and unusual mixture of warts-and-all family portraiture, subtle exposé of class and privilege, and minimalist depiction of a particular setting that’s rendered with an almost miraculously tactile sense of presence, photographer and filmmaker Victoria Hely-Hutchinson’s VACANCES is a deceptively unassuming film. Filmed over the course of a decade at the property in Provence inhabited by Hely-Hutchinson’s outrageously uninhibited grandmother, a bohemian Austro-Hungarian countess and family matriarch, VACANCES grew out of Hely-Hutchinson’s 2016 short film of the same name, and is something of a filmic complement to her autobiographical 2023 book, “I Left My Grandmother’s House”. The documentary delves, with a grace and open-endedness that belies its analytical bite, into both the bigger-than-life personality of “granny” as well as the sometimes strained dynamics among the rest of the family, including Hely-Hutchinson’s grandfather, mother, and siblings. Unique in suggesting by turns cinema vérité, reality TV, chamber theater, and the minimalism of landscape cinema, VACANCES is a profoundly singular work – a film whose technique is nearly invisible, but which sneaks up on you with its trenchant perceptions, layered meanings, and emotional and filmic complexity. “This time-lapse film, shot over a period of ten years, follows members of several generations of a wealthy aristocratic family with Austro-Hungarian roots. The entire film is set in a Provençal villa, whose social heart is the swimming pool, around which the women gather to exchange various observations and, surreptitiously, gossip. The center of the family is the aging matriarch, who likes to talk about her extravagant, promiscuous life, but at the same time commands all the attention and authority of those around her. However, her influence gradually weakens with each passing generation.” –JI.HLAVA INTERNATIONAL DOCUMENTARY FILM FESTIVAL

title: Haruki Murakami in Conversation + Tony Takitani (U)
description: We are honoured to welcome the celebrated Japanese author on stage to read aloud from his book The City and Its Uncertain Walls (2023) and discuss his work with interviewer Simon McBurney.

title: Black Swan
description: Nina, a ballerina, gets the chance to play the White Swan, Princess Odette. But she finds herself slipping into madness when Thomas, the artistic director, decides that Lily might fit the role better.

title: VIKA KIRCHENBAUER PGM 1
description: We enter this program with a salacious direct address-cum-invitation in PLEASE RELAX NOW, as Kirchenbauer seduces the viewer from a black box void, stretching the edges of imagination. In LIKE RATS LEAVING A SINKING SHIP, Kirchenbauer layers psychiatric assessments to consider the coherency of a biography, and assess the ways in which individual memory is puppeted by state apparatuses. Both SHE WHOSE BLOOD IS CLOTTING IN MY UNDERWEAR and MOOD MANAGEMENT again push the viewer’s capacity to render a coherent picture of actions, generating a half-constructed image which lends itself only then to a projection. Both works are guided by Kirchenbauer’s music project, COOL FOR YOU. Through essay and material vignettes, UNTITLED SEQUENCE OF GAPS explores light outside of the visible spectrum to consider violence as it attaches to different kinds of visibility and invisibility. To tickle is a form of touch, an intimate act carried out to delight, to excite, or to torment. In THE ISLAND OF PERPETUAL TICKLING (III), Kirchenbauer surrenders to this metaphoric and literal tickle. Noting that it is impossible to tickle oneself, her task requires assistance. PLEASE RELAX NOW (2014, 12 min, DCP) LIKE RATS LEAVING A SINKING SHIP (2012, 24.5 min, DCP) SHE WHOSE BLOOD IS CLOTTING IN MY UNDERWEAR (2016, 3.5 min, DCP) MOOD MANAGEMENT 2017, 2 min, DCPUNTITLED SEQUENCE OF GAPS (2020, 12.5 min, DCP) THE ISLAND OF PERPETUAL TICKLING (III) (2018, 13 min, DCP) Total running time: ca. 75 min. Filmmaker Vika Kirchenbauer in person for both screenings!

title: VIKA KIRCHENBAUER PGM 2
description: In the second program of our 2-part retrospective devoted to Vika Kirchenbauer, we dive deeper into the politics of labor in contemporary art, as the artist offers us a WELCOME ADDRESS, directly calling into question the art economy’s coded-progressive positioning of difference and diversity as symbolic cultural currency. Considering the foul, late-stage capitalist “Experience Economy,” YOU ARE BORING troubles the nature of looking. THE CAPACITY FOR ADEQUATE ANGER positions still images from the artist’s presumable childhood archive, gaps of nothingness, and the essay form to offer a critique of the production of contemporary art in the face of upward mobility, mapping subjectivity and political agency. To close this program with a thorough and considered look at the complicit role of artists and art institutions, COMPASSION AND INCONVENIENCE takes us back to 18th century London to trace the first public exhibitions of contemporary art, when materiality intersects with ideology via Liberalism and Enlightenment, taking to task the economic and colonial interests that define/d the “pursuit of refinement.” WELCOME ADDRESS (2017, 9 min, DCP) YOU ARE BORING! (2015, 14 min, DCP) THE CAPACITY FOR ADEQUATE ANGER (2021, 15 min, DCP) COMPASSION AND INCONVENIENCE (2024, 30 min, DCP) Total running time: ca. 75 min. Filmmaker Vika Kirchenbauer in person for both screenings!

title: Perfect Blue
description: "THE COLOUR OF ILLUSION IS PERFECT BLUE" A young Japanese singer is encouraged by her agent to quit singing and pursue an acting career, beginning with a role in a murder mystery TV show.

title: Possession
description: After Anna (Isabelle Adjani) reveals to her husband, Mark (Sam Neill), that she is having an affair, she leaves him and their son. Mark is devastated, and seeks out Heinrich (Heinz Bennent), the man who cuckolded him, only to receive a beating. After a series of violent confrontations between Mark and Anna, Mark hires a private investigator to follow her. Anna descends into madness, and it's soon clear that she is hiding a much bigger secret -- one that is both inexplicable and shocking.

title: The Craft
description: After transferring to a Los Angeles high school, Sarah (Robin Tunney) finds that her telekinetic gift appeals to a group of three wannabe witches, who happen to be seeking a fourth member for their rituals. Bonnie (Neve Campbell), Rochelle (Rachel True) and Nancy (Fairuza Balk), like Sarah herself, all have troubled backgrounds, which combined with their nascent powers lead to dangerous consequences. When a minor spell causes a fellow student to lose her hair, the girls grow power-mad.

title: Invasion of the Body Snatchers (1956)
description: * ON SALE 28th SEPT * In the sleepy Californian town of Santa Mira, strange happenings are afoot. Dr. Miles Bennell finds residents experiencing an epidemic of mass hysteria, imagining their relatives replaced by detached, emotionless copies. As Bennell gets closer to the horrifying truth - that the substitutions are part of an extraterrestrial invasion scheme and the copies are emerging from giant seed pods - the 'pod people' begin to close in.

title: Under the Skin (2013)
description: An alien entity inhabits the earthly form of a seductive young woman who combs the Scottish highways in search of the human prey it is here to plunder. It lures its isolated and forsaken male victims into an otherworldly dimension where they are stripped and consumed. But life in all its complexity starts to change the alien. It begins to see itself as 'she', as human, with tragic and terrifying consequences.

title: The Third Part of the Night
description: The screening on the 12th of October will feature an introduction by writer Michael Brooke. The first feature by Andrzej Żuławski…

title: The Thing
description: In remote Antarctica, a group of American research scientists are disturbed at their base camp by a helicopter shooting at a sled dog. When they take in the dog, it brutally attacks both human beings and canines in the camp and they discover that the beast can assume the shape of its victims. A resourceful helicopter pilot (Kurt Russell) and the camp doctor (Richard Dysart) lead the camp crew in a desperate, gory battle against the vicious creature before it picks them all off, one by one.

title: Cosi Fan Tutte
description: The Met: Live in HD season kicks off with Mozart’s satirical comedy of fickle young love, one of the composer’s most sublime creations.

title: Suspiria [1977]
description: Suzy (Jessica Harper) travels to Germany to attend ballet school. When she arrives, late on a stormy night, no one lets her in, and she sees Pat (Eva Axén), another student, fleeing from the school. When Pat reaches her apartment, she is murdered. The next day, Suzy is admitted to her new school, but has a difficult time settling in. She hears noises, and often feels ill. As more people die, Suzy uncovers the terrifying secret history of the place.

title: In The Mood For Love
description: In 1962 Hong Kong, neighbors Su Li-zhen (Mrs. Chan) and Chow Mo-wan (Mr. Chow) discover their spouses are having an affair. As they spend time together, they develop feelings for each other, but their relationship remains chaste and unspoken, reflecting societal constraints and their own moral compass.

title: Jennifer's Body
description: When a demon takes possession of her, high-school hottie Jennifer (Megan Fox) turns a hungry eye on guys who never stood a chance with her before. While evil Jennifer satisfies her appetite for human flesh with the school's male population, her nerdy friend, Needy (Amanda Seyfried), learns what's happening and vows to put an end to the carnage.

title: Funeral Parade presents A Nightmare on Elm Street 2: Freddy's Revenge
description: Jesse Walsh (Mark Patton) moves with his family into the home of the lone survivor from a series of attacks by dream-stalking monster Freddy Krueger (Robert Englund). There, Jesse is bedeviled by nightmares and inexplicably violent impulses. It turns out Freddy needs a host body to carry out his gruesome vendetta against the youth of Springwood, Ohio. While Freddy gains influence, Jesse and his girlfriend, Lisa (Kim Myers), race against the clock trying to figure out what’s going on. The follow up to the film that introduced Freddy Krueger into our nightmares has become an iconically queer film due to its not so subtle context, tones and explicit desires. With intro from film curator Sarah Cleary.

title: AVATARS: THE DOMINATRIX SLEEPS TONIGHT
description: Taking the avatar of the dominatrix as its starting point, this short film program gathers together various films made – across a 40-year period – by or in collaboration with those who have experience in the leathersex scene. As an avatar of working sex, the figure of the dominatrix is elusive in so far as she uses the theater of the scene of “violation” to both pursue and obfuscate her desires. Though cinema longs to unmask the dominatrix to witness her “true” self, this program instead finds pleasure in the artifice of the scene wherein various characters find themselves at the mercy of the seductive and controlling gaze of the dominatrix. The shorts here range from documentary exercises of sadism, like Ione Wang’s WHEN I LOOK AT YOU, I SEE ME, to the electric pop-music video work of Beth B’s THE DOMINATRIX SLEEPS TONIGHT, made for the band Dominatrix. Shorts by Azian Nurudin and Michelle Handelman from the late 1980s and early 1990s invite a reconsideration of race, power, and aesthetics through their respectively overlooked and censored films, while M.M. Serra and Maria Beatty’s work demonstrates the aesthetic bliss that emerges from submitting to the fantasies of a powerful woman. Azian Nurudin NANCY’S NIGHTMARE (1988, 5 min, digital) Michelle Handelman CATSCAN (1989, 6 min, Super-8mm-to-digital. Made with with Monte Cazazza.) M.M. Serra & Jennifer Reeves DARLING INTERNATIONAL (1999, 22 min, 16mm-to-digital) Maria Beatty THE BLACK GLOVE (1996, 30 min, digital) Beth B THE DOMINATRIX SLEEPS TONIGHT (1984, 4 min, video) Ione Wang WHEN I LOOK AT YOU, I SEE ME (2024, 7 min, digital) Total running time: ca. 80 min.

description: Jack Torrance (Jack Nicholson) becomes winter caretaker at the isolated Overlook Hotel in Colorado, hoping to cure his writer's block. He settles in along with his wife, Wendy (Shelley Duvall), and his son, Danny (Danny Lloyd), who is plagued by psychic premonitions. As Jack's writing goes nowhere and Danny's visions become more disturbing, Jack discovers the hotel's dark secrets and begins to unravel into a homicidal maniac hell-bent on terrorizing his family.

title: SEDUCTION: THE CRUEL WOMAN
description: In SEDUCTION: THE CRUEL WOMAN, Wanda is a dominatrix and gallerist who invites patrons to witness her scenes with her submissives. Inspired by the Marquis de Sade’s “Venus in Furs”, writer-directors Monika Treut and Elfi Mikesch spin Sade’s tale of power, apathy, and pleasure to foreground the role the spectator (both imagined and real) plays in enabling these violating acts to occur.

title: The Texas Chain Saw Massacre
description: When Sally (Marilyn Burns) hears that her grandfather's grave may have been vandalized, she and her paraplegic brother, Franklin (Paul A. Partain), set out with their friends to investigate. After a detour to their family's old farmhouse, they discover a group of crazed, murderous outcasts living next door. As the group is attacked one by one by the chainsaw-wielding Leatherface (Gunnar Hansen), who wears a mask of human skin, the survivors must do everything they can to escape.

title: Mikey and Nicky
description: Elaine May crafted a gangster film like no other in the nocturnal odyssey Mikey and Nicky, capitalising on the chemistry between frequent collaborators John Cassavetes and Peter Falk by casting them together as small-time mobsters whose lifelong relationship has turned sour. Set over the course of one night, this restless drama finds Nicky (Cassavetes) holed up in a hotel after the boss he stole money from puts a hit out on him. Terrified, he calls on Mikey (Falk), the one person he thinks can save him. Scripted to match the live-wire energy of its stars—alongside supporting players Ned Beatty, Joyce Van Patten, and Carol Grace—and inspired by real-life characters from May’s own childhood, this unbridled portrait of male friendship turned tragic is an unsung masterpiece of American cinema. Mikey and Nicky on 14th October is featured as part of Gangsters Have Feelings Too, a season exploring the sensitive gangster film. The season is presented with the National Film and Television School’s Film Studies, Programming and Curation MA.

However, on the night of her engagement party, a young boy named Sean (Cameron Bright) turns up, saying he is her dead husband reincarnated. At first she ignores the child, but his knowledge of her former husband's life is uncanny, leading her to believe that he might be telling the truth.

title: NARROW ROOMS: LES FANTÔMES DU HARD + FISTULE
description: Most kinky queers in NYC know all about the Mineshaft, the legendary, long-shuttered NYC sex club in the Meatpacking District that was in operation from 1976 to 1985. But across the Atlantic, France’s first “hard” gay BDSM sex club was also called Mineshaft, and it has remained a sacred space for BDSM and fetish sex in Marseille since its opening in 1967. In this pair of short experimental documentaries, director Lazare Lazarus and friends excavate the archive left by the Mineshaft’s founder Jean-Pierre Fouque. Chapter 1 tells the story of the squatters who took over Fouque’s apartment after his death in 2022 and discovered his archive, while illuminating aspects of the club owner’s life – his lovers, political views, activism, and more. Chapter 2, co-directed with Lupa Charon Gateff, is more of a found-footage experimental porno mixtape, using the Mineshaft’s archive of hardcore gay porn and BDSM videotapes to take us into the dungeons of Europe, both real and imagined. These two shorts will be followed by Emre Busse’s FISTULE, which invites the audience into a realm where an anal fissure serves as a dramatic springboard, exposing the absurdity of societal norms with a mix of tragedy, camp, and sexuality. If you’re a fan of the films of Liz Purchell (ASK ANY BUDDY), Ryan A. White (RAW! UNCUT! VIDEO!), and Yann Gonzalez (KNIFE + HEART), you’ll find much to enjoy in this month’s program. Lazare Lazarus LES FANTÔMES DU HARD, CHAPTER 1 2023, 35 min, DCP. In French with English subtitles. Lazare Lazarus & Lupa Charon Gateff LES FANTÔMES DU HARD, CHAPTER 2 2024, 24 min, DCP. In French with English subtitles. Emre Busse FISTULE 2026, 17 min, DCP Total running time: ca 80 min.

description: Academy Award® winner Nicole Kidman (Best Actress, The Hours, 2003) delivers an unforgettable performance in this gothic supernatural thriller. In 1945, Grace (Kidman) and her two children wait for her husband's return from the war, living an unusually isolated existence behind the locked doors and drawn curtains of a secluded mansion in Jersey. Three mysterious new servants arrive and it becomes chillingly clear that there is far more to this house than can be seen, and Grace finds herself in a terrifying fight to save her children and preserve her sanity. Acclaimed by critics, the unpredictable twists and turns of this compelling psychological horror classic will keep you on the edge of your seat.

HALLOWEEN II (1981): After failing to kill stubborn survivor Laurie and taking a bullet or six from former psychiatrist Dr. Sam Loomis, Michael Myers has followed Laurie to the Haddonfield Memorial Hospital, where she’s been admitted for Myers’ attempt on her life. The institution proves to be particularly suited to serial killers, however, as Myers cuts, stabs and slashes his way through hospital staff to reach his favourite victim. title: MULTI-MEDIA RESOURCE CENTER PGM 1: CONFESSIONS AND SEX HISTORIES
description: The openness and non-judgement that characterized the National Sex Forum meant that the films it produced depicted not only sex acts without scripting or simulation, but also frank discussions of participants’ sexual desires and experiences. Most straightforward in its treatment of these discussions is WARDELL POMEROY TAKES A SEX HISTORY, in which the titular doctor and former Alfred Kinsey collaborator interviews sexologist-in-training Janice Epp on her past relationships, sexual preferences, childhood awareness of puberty, present-day masturbation habits, and other aspects of her sexual identity. In this program, SEX HISTORY is accompanied by three more erotic portraits, each of them both candid and playful. title: MULTI-MEDIA RESOURCE CENTER PGM 2: ACTIVE PARTNERS
description: ACTIVE PARTNERS: FOUR FILMS ON SEX AND DISABILITY Reflecting on the National Sex Forum (NSF) and Multi-Media Resource Center (MMRC), Ted McIlvenna often said that his proudest achievement was his work producing films on the sexuality of people with disabilities. These films dealt frankly with a subject seldom addressed either in erotic and sexually explicit cinema or in educational media about physical disability. They used a combination of candid narration and explicit visuals to explore the possibilities of sexual expression for disabled people, particularly those with able-bodied partners. The first two films in this program were directed by Laird Sutton for the NSF, while the latter two were produced by the University of Minnesota and San Francisco State University, and distributed by the MMRC. description: (STACHKA) Eisenstein’s interest in the Freudian father complex drives this psychological scenario in which non-actors step forward to acknowledge the viewer, illustrating Eisenstein’s desire to penetrate to the heart of cinema, sidestepping realism by ‘being real.’ Governmental restrictions made STRIKE the only completed film of a series intended to portray the road to revolution.

title: MULTI-MEDIA RESOURCE CENTER PGM 3: GAY LIBERATION ON 16MM
description: From the late 1960s through the early 1980s, politically active gay and lesbian filmmakers like Arthur J. Bressan, Jr. and the Mariposa Film Group made didactic agitprop documentaries and narrative films on the liberation movement taking place in the streets around them. But alongside these works were smaller – in scope, length, and film gauge – and often more experimental works that shed light on the ideology of gay liberation in a less didactic mode. The two films in this program directed by Laird Sutton for the National Sex Forum take the form of casual, unstructured conversations between trios of gay men and lesbians. The others – which were, apart from FREEDOM DAY PARADE, distributed by the Multi-Media Resource Center – use documentary and satire to explore the concerns and culture of the gay liberation movement. Wakefield Poole FREEDOM DAY PARADE (1974, 11 min, 16mm-to-DCP) Laird Sutton GAY WOMEN SPEAK (1979, 15 min, 16mm. Featuring Phyllis Lyon.) Laird Sutton A GAY VIEW: MALE (1975, 17 min, 16mm) Sharrie Farrell SANDY & MADELINE’S FAMILY (1973, 30 min, 16mm) Jan Oxenberg A COMEDY IN SIX UNNATURAL ACTS (1975, 27 min, 16mm-to-DCP) Total running time: ca. 105 min.

title: Scream 3
description: As bodies begin dropping around the set of 'STAB 3', a movie sequel based on the gruesome Woodsboro killings, Sidney Prescott and the other survivors are once again drawn into a game of a horror movie mayhem.

title: EC: BATTLESHIP POTEMKIN
description: (BRONENOSETS POTEMKIN) “POTEMKIN used [Eisenstein’s] new set of rules to create what has been called the most perfect and concise example of film structure. Like STRIKE, [POTEMKIN] has no hero, only the masses, and no plot, only an incident plucked from the pre-history of the Revolution.” –Standish Lawder, EISENSTEIN AND CONSTRUCTIVISM “POTEMKIN was the first work to embody, in their most tangible form, various principles of construction peculiar to the medium: montage (or editing) and parallel action (the expansion of time through spatial manipulation); or, in sum, the purely formal deployment of objective action to create psychological dimensions. Eisenstein was not the first ‘film artist,’ but he was the first to be so pure, the first to use photography like painting in movement, photography like verbal imagery. As set down in his writings, his own theories inform us of this. Yet POTEMKIN must be seen to be believed.” –Parker Tyler

title: Scream 4
description: Fifteen years after the original Woodsboro murders, Sidney Prescott returns home to promote her new book about surviving trauma, only for a new Ghostface killer to emerge, targeting a new group of teens.

title: MULTI-MEDIA RESOURCE CENTER PGM 4: WOMEN’S LIB
description: THE PERSONAL AND THE POLITICAL: SEXUALITY, ROMANCE AND WOMEN’S LIB This program uses the cliché adage of second-wave feminism as a conceptual framework, bringing together films focused on individual and paired bodies with those concerned with the social and the political. Two playful Multi-Media Resource Center (MMRC) shorts that use visual and narrative tools to invert expectations of heterosexual gender performance are followed by films from the MMRC catalog (SELF-HEALTH, HOOKERS) and the Los Angeles underground (HIDDEN MEMORIES, I DON’T KNOW), departing in key ways from doctrinaire women’s liberation ideology. In these films, sexuality, romance, physical health, and communal solidarity are woven into a patchwork that renders women’s political and social identities more multifaceted than either dominant patriarchy or the mainstream feminist movement envisaged. Sam Joseph & Mariko Tse FIRST DATE (1977, 5 min, 8mm-to-DCP) Anne Severson I CHANGE I AM THE SAME (1969, 1 min, 16mm) Catherine Allen, Judy Irola, Allie Light, and Joan Musante SELF-HEALTH (1974, 23 min, 16mm-to-DCP) Jacqueline Frazier HIDDEN MEMORIES (1977, 10 min, 16mm-to-DCP) Penelope Spheeris I DON’T KNOW (1970, 20 min, 16mm-to-DCP) George Csicsery HOOKERS (1975, 25 min, 16mm) Total running time: ca. 90 min.

title: The Exorcist (Extended Cut)
description: One of the most profitable horror movies ever made, this tale of an exorcism is based loosely on actual events. When young Regan (Linda Blair) starts acting odd -- levitating, speaking in tongues -- her worried mother (Ellen Burstyn) seeks medical help, only to hit a dead end. A local priest (Jason Miller), however, thinks the girl may be seized by the devil. The priest makes a request to perform an exorcism, and the church sends in an expert (Max von Sydow) to help with the difficult job.

title: Dance Umbrella Sunday Shorts: Spaces of Encounter (15*)
description: A programme of shorts selected by Omar Rajeh , bringing together works that explore the relationship between body, memory and place, revealing the social, political and emotional landscapes we inhabit.

title: The Thing
description: In remote Antarctica, a group of American research scientists are disturbed at their base camp by a helicopter shooting at a sled dog. When they take in the dog, it brutally attacks both human beings and canines in the camp and they discover that the beast can assume the shape of its victims. A resourceful helicopter pilot (Kurt Russell) and the camp doctor (Richard Dysart) lead the camp crew in a desperate, gory battle against the vicious creature before it picks them all off, one by one.

title: EC: OLD AND NEW
description: (STAROYE I NOVOYE) With OLD AND NEW, also known as THE GENERAL LINE, Eisenstein developed and perfected his theories of “mise-en-cadre,” using the montage of characters in the foreground and background to conjure meanings, and “overtonal montage,” bringing silent film to its zenith.

title: RETURN TO THE TATLER + VARIETY
description: As part of our anniversary celebrations, we take a detour into the Rio’s saucy 1970’s years as the Dalston Tatler, one of London’s highest grossing porn cinema clubs with an uncensored grindhouse programme and a full burlesque striptease extravaganza stage show.  We delve into the lurid stories and ...

title: The Shining [UK Version]
description: Jack Torrance (Jack Nicholson) becomes winter caretaker at the isolated Overlook Hotel in Colorado, hoping to cure his writer's block. He settles in along with his wife, Wendy (Shelley Duvall), and his son, Danny (Danny Lloyd), who is plagued by psychic premonitions. As Jack's writing goes nowhere and Danny's visions become more disturbing, Jack discovers the hotel's dark secrets and begins to unravel into a homicidal maniac hell-bent on terrorizing his family.

title: MULTI-MEDIA RESOURCE CENTER PGM 5: BROUGHTON EC+
description: James Broughton, prolific poet-filmmaker and member of Anthology’s own Essential Cinema Selection Committee, was one of many Bay Area experimental filmmakers whose work was distributed by the Multi-Media Resource Center. Generally advertised in the “Erotic Fantasy” section of the distributor’s catalogs, Broughton’s films were recontextualized by their inclusion, their sensuality and spirituality understood as components of a holistic understanding of sexuality for the sex educator or therapist. In this special edition of Anthology’s Broughton Essential Cinema program, three characteristic works of the filmmaker’s late 60s-early 70s output are preceded by a very special entry in the National Sex Forum filmography, in which Broughton himself is bathed and massaged by erotic masseur Kenneth Ray Stubbs. Laird Sutton JAMES (1979, 10 min, 16mm) James Broughton THE BED (1968, 19 min, 16mm) James Broughton NUPTIAE (1969, 14 min, 16mm) James Broughton THE GOLDEN POSITIONS (1970, 32 min, 16mm) Total running time: ca. 80 min.

title: EC: OCTOBER
description: (OKTYABR) “An imaginary document projected on actual locations, OCTOBER is the Soviet equivalent of the Sistine Chapel – an artist commissioned by the state has represented the sacred origins of the universe. Woodrow Wilson had famously hailed D.W. Griffith’s THE BIRTH OF A NATION (1915) as ‘history written with lightning,’ but Eisenstein’s cosmic newsreel cum theoretical film poem goes beyond THE BIRTH OF A NATION, as well as his own BATTLESHIP POTEMKIN, in drafting the past to serve the requirements of the present. No less than the revolutionaries who made October, Eisenstein understood himself as history’s tool. Thus consecrated to the Bolshevik faith, his OCTOBER is a perfect tautology – it clarifies and improves on history in the service of objective historical necessity.” –J. Hoberman, THE RED ATLANTIS: COMMUNIST CULTURE IN THE ABSENCE OF COMMUNISM

title: MULTI-MEDIA RESOURCE CENTER PGM 6: EROTIC FANTASY
description: EROTIC FANTASY: BEESON AND BEYOND While the bulk of the National Sex Forum’s (NSF) in-house productions were directed by Laird Sutton, a Methodist minister like co-founder Ted McIlvenna, the organization’s more experimental output was mostly helmed by Constance (or Coni) Beeson. A photojournalist-turned-filmmaker, Beeson’s films on women’s sexuality were cited as inspirations by her contemporary Barbara Hammer. In this program, presented in chronological order, three Beeson films produced for the NSF, each depicting sexual encounters layered in double-exposure and pastoral imagery, are bookended by classic works of expressive erotic cinema that, though not distributed by the Multi-Media Resource Center, would be at home in its catalogs. José Rodriguez-Soltero JEROVI (1965, 11 min, 16mm. Preserved by Anthology Film Archives with support from the Andy Warhol Foundation for the Visual Arts.) Coni Beeson THE NOW (1970, 14 min, 16mm) Coni Beeson HOLDING (1971, 15 min, 16mm) Coni Beeson STAMEN (1972, 15 min, 16mm) Chick Strand FEVER DREAM (1979, 7 min, 16mm) Total running time: ca. 65 min.

title: Possession
description: After Anna (Isabelle Adjani) reveals to her husband, Mark (Sam Neill), that she is having an affair, she leaves him and their son. Mark is devastated, and seeks out Heinrich (Heinz Bennent), the man who cuckolded him, only to receive a beating. After a series of violent confrontations between Mark and Anna, Mark hires a private investigator to follow her. Anna descends into madness, and it's soon clear that she is hiding a much bigger secret -- one that is both inexplicable and shocking.

title: MULTI-MEDIA RESOURCE CENTER PGM 7: PATTERN FILMS, PART 1
description: The majority of Laird Sutton’s work for the National Sex Forum (NSF) consisted of “pattern films,” so termed for their portrayal of a real couple’s (or individual’s, or group’s) sexual pattern. According to a 1979 NSF brochure, “actors are not used in these films; the participants are ordinary people behaving and responding sexually as they usually do…. The persons to be filmed are interviewed about their sexual patterns. Once sexual activity commences, no directions are given. Every effort is made to allow the individuals to feel at ease.” Reflecting their use in structured therapeutic sessions, this selection of pattern films is preceded by a short from the Multi-Media Resource Center’s “Humor and Mood Alteration” collection, meant to dispel unease ahead of these candid portraits. Greg Von Buchau LOVE TOAD (1971, 2 min, 16mm-to-DCP) Laird Sutton POSSIBILITIES (1973, 12 min, 16mm) Laird Sutton QUIET AFTERNOON (1975, 20 min, 16mm) Edd Dundas NICK AND JON (1976, 20 min, 16mm) Laird Sutton BOTH/AND (1975, 25 min, 16mm) Total running time: ca. 85 min.

title: Frankenstein (1931) and The Bride of Frankenstein (1935)
description: FRANKENSTEIN (1931): Henry Frankenstein pieces together body parts in the hope of bringing a human-like creature to life. The mad scientist’s dreams are shattered by his monstrous creation awakening with rage to a world that hates and fears him. THE BRIDE OF FRANKENSTEIN (1935): Dr. Frankenstein and his monster both turn out to be alive after being attacked by an angry mob. The now-chastened scientist attempts to escape his past, but a former mentor forces him to assist with the creation of a new creature. Presented with a 10-minute break between features.

title: Mulholland Dr.
description: A dark-haired woman (Laura Elena Harring) is left amnesiac after a car crash. She wanders the streets of Los Angeles in a daze before taking refuge in an apartment. There she is discovered by Betty (Naomi Watts), a wholesome Midwestern blonde who has come to the City of Angels seeking fame as an actress. Together, the two attempt to solve the mystery of Rita's true identity. The story is set in a dream-like Los Angeles, spoilt neither by traffic jams nor smog.

title: Carrie
description: In this chilling adaptation of Stephen King's horror novel, withdrawn and sensitive teen Carrie White (Sissy Spacek) faces taunting from classmates at school and abuse from her fanatically pious mother (Piper Laurie) at home. When strange occurrences start happening around Carrie, she begins to suspect that she has supernatural powers. Invited to the prom by the empathetic Tommy Ross (William Katt), Carrie tries to let her guard down, but things eventually take a dark and violent turn.

title: An American Werewolf in London
description: David (David Naughton) and Jack (Griffin Dunne), two American college students, are backpacking through Britain when a large wolf attacks them. David survives with a bite, but Jack is brutally killed. As David heals in the hospital, he's plagued by violent nightmares of his mutilated friend, who warns David that he is becoming a werewolf. When David discovers the horrible truth, he contemplates committing suicide before the next full moon causes him to transform from man to murderous beast.

title: The Blair Witch Project
description: Found video footage tells the tale of three film students (Heather Donahue, Joshua Leonard, Michael C. Williams) who've traveled to a small town to collect documentary footage about the Blair Witch, a legendary local murderer. Over the course of several days, the students interview townspeople and gather clues to support the tale's veracity. But the project takes a frightening turn when the students lose their way in the woods and begin hearing horrific noises.

title: Cruising
description: There’s a killer on the loose in New York City, and he’s targeting gay men in the West Village. Fortunately for the NYPD, he’s got a type – slim, dark-haired, handsome – and officer Steve Burns (Al Pacino) fits the bill. To crack the case, Steve must journey into the city’s nocturnal underworld of S&M and leather bars, hoping to catch the killer’s eye – but will he lose himself along the way? Controversial with both straight and gay audiences upon its initial release, Friedkin’s film still retains its power to shock and unsettle 45 years later.

title: The Witch
description: In 1630 New England, panic and despair envelops a farmer, his wife and their children when youngest son Samuel suddenly vanishes. The family blames Thomasin, the oldest daughter who was watching the boy at the time of his disappearance. With suspicion and paranoia mounting, twin siblings Mercy and Jonas suspect Thomasin of witchcraft, testing the clan's faith, loyalty and love to one another.

title: Seven
description: GLUTTONY. GREED. SLOTH. WRATH. PRIDE. LUST. ENVY. Two cops (Brad Pitt and Morgan Freeman) track a brilliant and elusive killer who orchestrates a string of horrific murders, each kill targeting a practitioner of one of the Seven Deadly Sins. Gwyneth Paltrow also stars in this acclaimed thriller set in a dour, drizzly city sick with pain and blight. David Fincher (Fight Club, Zodiac, The Curious Case of Benjamin Button) guides the action - physical, mental and spiritual - with a sure understanding of what terrifies us, right up to a stunning denouement that will rip the scar tissue off the most hardened soul. The 4K restoration of “Se7en” was completed at Warner Bros. Discovery’s Motion Picture Imaging and sourced from the original camera negative. The restoration was overseen by David Fincher.

title: The Innocents (1961)
description: In Victorian England, the uncle of orphaned niece Flora and nephew Miles hires Miss Giddens as governess to raise the children at his estate with total independence and authority. Soon after her arrival, Miss Giddens comes to believe that the spirits of the former governess Miss Jessel and valet Peter Quint are possessing the children. Miss Giddens decides to help the children to face and exorcise the spirits.

description: Fifteen years after murdering his sister on Halloween Night 1963, Michael Myers escapes from a mental hospital and returns to the small town of Haddonfield, Illinois to kill again.

title: In The Mood For Love
description: In 1962 Hong Kong, neighbors Su Li-zhen (Mrs. Chan) and Chow Mo-wan (Mr. Chow) discover their spouses are having an affair. As they spend time together, they develop feelings for each other, but their relationship remains chaste and unspoken, reflecting societal constraints and their own moral compass.

title: Halloween II (1981)
description: After failing to kill stubborn survivor Laurie and taking a bullet or six from former psychiatrist Dr. Sam Loomis, Michael Myers has followed Laurie to the Haddonfield Memorial Hospital, where she's been admitted for Myers' attempt on her life. The institution proves to be particularly suited to serial killers, however, as Myers cuts, stabs and slashes his way through hospital staff to reach his favorite victim.

title: Halloween III: Season of the Witch
description: After a terrified toy salesman is mysteriously attacked and brought to the hospital clutching the year's most popular Halloween mask, Dr. Daniel Challis sets out to investigate the strange events and finds himself thrust into a nightmarish conspiracy.

title: EC: IVAN THE TERRIBLE: PARTS 1 & 2
description: “The first time in history a man has committed suicide by cinema,” quipped Dovzhenko. A state-sanctioned production, Ivan’s opulent furs and jewels color the black-and-white machinations by a demonic Czar bent on making his subjects’ lives a living hell – a statement pointed with outrage directly at Stalin.

title: The Others
description: Academy Award® winner Nicole Kidman (Best Actress, The Hours, 2003) delivers an unforgettable performance in this gothic supernatural thriller. In 1945, Grace (Kidman) and her two children wait for her husband's return from the war, living an unusually isolated existence behind the locked doors and drawn curtains of a secluded mansion in Jersey. Three mysterious new servants arrive and it becomes chillingly clear that there is far more to this house than can be seen, and Grace finds herself in a terrifying fight to save her children and preserve her sanity. Acclaimed by critics, the unpredictable twists and turns of this compelling psychological horror classic will keep you on the edge of your seat.

title: The Sacrifice
description: Andrei Tarkovsky’s visionary final film unfolds in the hours before a nuclear holocaust. Erland Josephson, in an award-winning role, plays retired actor Alexander who is celebrating his birthday with family and friends when a crackly TV announcement warns of an imminent nuclear catastrophe. Alexander makes a promise to God that he will sacrifice all he holds dear, if the disaster can be averted. The next day dawns and, as if in a dream, everything is restored to normality. But Alexander must keep his vow. Among many other awards, The Sacrifice won the Cannes Grand Prix in 1986, the same year that Tarkovsky died of cancer in Paris at the age of 54.

title: Suspiria [1977]
description: Suzy (Jessica Harper) travels to Germany to attend ballet school. When she arrives, late on a stormy night, no one lets her in, and she sees Pat (Eva Axén), another student, fleeing from the school. When Pat reaches her apartment, she is murdered. The next day, Suzy is admitted to her new school, but has a difficult time settling in. She hears noises, and often feels ill. As more people die, Suzy uncovers the terrifying secret history of the place.

My viola takes on the voice of the occult-obsessed lecturer(/director), possessed by the alluring darkness of the subject, wrestling with the film’s message of hierarchal corruption and its prevailing controversies . Please view this YouTube video for a sample of Hugo's work.

title: ROSALYN DREXLER: WHO DOES SHE THINK SHE IS?
description: Rosalyn Drexler (1926-2025) was a category-defying creative force. Over the course of her multidecade career, she worked as a painter (creating some of the first examples of Pop art), a novelist, an Obie-award-winning playwright, a film critic, an occasional nightclub singer, and briefly, a professional wrestler. The documentary WHO DOES SHE THINK SHE IS? (1975) provides a window into Drexler’s extraordinary creative universe. Set against the backdrop of the lost artistic demimonde of 20th-century New York, the film – directed by Patricia Lewis Jaffe and Gaby Rodgers – shows the artist rehearsing her madcap cabaret performances, cooking for her family in her art-strewn Manhattan apartment, and speaking candidly about her art, writing, and life. As Newsweek critic Jack Kroll remarks in the film, “[Drexler’s] essential insight is that people and things are completely insane, and she speaks from inside the whale.” The documentary will be accompanied by never-before-seen home movies shot by Drexler and her husband Sherman in the 1940-50s, as well as a panel discussion. The screening coincides with a major exhibition of her work from the 1960s at Garth Greenan Gallery at 25 Greene Street; for more info about the exhibition visit: https://www.garthgreenan.com/

title: Solve Along A Murder She Wrote

Watch as Cabot Cove gets caught up in a murder mystery only JB Fletcher (or you!) can solve! Solve-Along-A-Murder-She-Wrote is a unique and hilarious night featuring games, prizes and audience participation, with special permission from NBC Universal Television. See the show Time Out rated one of 2021 and 2019’s 50 Great Nights Out in London that has played to sell-out audiences across the UK and Australia. Tim Benzie is obsessed with Murder, She Wrote, having watched the original series when it was first broadcast, and now relishing the repeats on television everywhere. Tim is the writer/performer of “It’s a Mystery!”, all about our love of whodunnits. An award-winning playwright and co-writer of the Royal Vauxhall Tavern’s 2017-2023 pantos (‘Goosed’, ‘Rubbed’, ‘Slipped’, ‘Pricked’, ‘Cracked’ and ‘Tossed’). He is the co-producer of the camp club night PopHorror.
